ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Importance Weighted KL Regularization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to experiment with a variant of KL regularization that uses importance weights, as proposed in the Importance Weighted Autoencoders (IWAE) paper, to estimate the marginal KL divergence between the fine-tuned and reference distributions. Specifically, we will use a series of importance samples, each with a probability computed based on the log-likelihoods of the fine-tuned model, to estimate the KL term in the KL-regularized objective. This approach avoids the need for computing the intractable marginal likelihoods of the diffusion process and allows us to leverage the power of reinforcement learning for fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Baselines include the standard PPO algorithm with a relaxed KL regularization (either ignored or based on trajectory KL), and we will also experiment with a population-based training of PPO with and without importance-weighted KL regularization.
COST: 330
PREDICTION: By leveraging the IWAE method, we expect to achieve stable and efficient fine-tuning of diffusion models, and our experiments might reveal that a properly implemented importance-weighted KL regularization provides a better trade-off between reward maximization and distribution alignment compared to standard KL regularization methods. The reliability of this approach might slightly decrease in settings where the reference model is not accurately provided or in high-dimensions.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploiting Denoising Process Structure for Better KL Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate how the structure of the denoising process in diffusion models can be exploited to improve the estimation of the marginal KL divergence between the fine-tuned and reference distributions. Specifically, we will divide the denoising process into smaller steps, and use a temporal markov blanket (TMB) representation to factorize the probability distribution over successive intermediate states. This will enable us to decompose the intractable marginal likelihood into a sum of tractable conditional likelihoods, each corresponding to a step in the denoising process.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with both importance-weighted KL regularization (IWKL) as proposed in our first experiment, and the TMB-based approach for approximating the marginal KL.
COST: 831
PREDICTION: We expect to show that the TMB-based approach provides a more accurate estimation of the marginal KL divergence, especially for models with complex denoising processes. However, it might also be more computationally expensive, potentially making it less suitable for large-scale settings.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Best-of-N Sampling for Efficient KL Regularization of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to experiment with using a Best-of-N sampling strategy as a means to approximate the KL regularization term in the fine-tuning objective for diffusion models. Specifically, we will use a logarithmic spacing to sample a set of N trajectory variants from the pre-trained diffusion model, and then select the top-K variants with the highest reward. We will then use these selected trajectories to approximate the KL regularization term, potentially providing a more efficient and robust alternative to current methods.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with both IWKL and the TMB-based approach as controls, and also explore how the choice of N and K influences the performance of the Best-of-N sampling strategy.
COST: 1170
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the Best-of-N sampling strategy provides a good trade-off between efficiency and accuracy, potentially making it a viable alternative to current KL regularization methods. However, it may also be sensitive to the choice of hyperparameters and the quality of the pre-trained diffusion model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Pre-training of Diffusion Models with Reconstruction and Denoising Tasks
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the benefits of unsupervised pre-training of diffusion models using a combination of reconstruction and denoising tasks. Specifically, we will train the diffusion model to learn a reversible transformation between a noisy input and a clean target, as well as learn to denoise a transformed version of the clean target. This can potentially improve the stability and performance of the model during fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: We will experiment with pre-training the diffusion models using random noise as input, and also use a real-world dataset (e.g. CIFAR-10 or LSUN) to investigate the benefits of self-supervised learning.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: We expect to find that pre-training the diffusion models with reconstruction and denoising tasks improves their stability and performance during fine-tuning, and also enables them to learn more complex and abstract representations of the data. However, it may also lead to overfitting if not properly regularized.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating No-Regret Learning for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to experiment with a no-regret learning approach for fine-tuning diffusion models. Specifically, we will use a multi-instance learning scheme, where the diffusion model is trained on a sequence of tasks, each with a different policy for selecting the fine-tuning objective. This can potentially lead to improved stability and performance, as the model can adapt to changing environments and task distributions.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed no-regret learning approach to standard reinforcement learning methods (e.g. PPO), as well as to a random policy that selects a fine-tuning objective uniformly at random.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the no-regret learning approach leads to improved stability and performance, especially in tasks with multiple objectives or nonlinear Reward Functions. However, it may also be sensitive to the choice of instance and may require a significant amount of exploration to converge to good solutions.

TITLE: Evaluating the Effect of Incorporating Flow Models into Diffusion Models for Improved Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose to experiment with incorporating flow models into diffusion models to improve fine-tuning. Specifically, we will use a diffusion-flow hybrid model, which combines the strengths of both diffusion and flow models to improve the stability and performance of fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed diffusion-flow hybrid model to standard diffusion models and flow models alone, as well as to other fine-tuning methods (e.g. KL-regularized PPO).
COST: 2332.8
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the diffusion-flow hybrid model leads to improved stability and performance, especially in tasks with nonlinear and complex data distributions. However, it may also be computationally more expensive due to the added complexity of the flow model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Sample Quality through Learning to Correct Pre-Training Errors without Explicit Rewards
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate a method for learning to correct pre-training errors in diffusion models without explicit rewards. Specifically, we will use a self-critic or self-supervised learning approach, where the model learns to predict its own errors and adjusts its internal state to correct them.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed self-critic approach to standard error correction methods (e.g. KL-regularized PPO with a pre-trained model) and to a random initialization.
COST: 2681.63
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the self-critic approach leads to improved sample quality, especially in tasks with complex and nonlinear data distributions. However, it may also be sensitive to the quality of the pre-training regime and may require a significant amount of exploration to converge to good solutions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging KL-Regularization for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We design an experiment where we compare the performance of three fine-tuning approaches for diffusion models: (1) KL-regularized reinforcement learning (PPO), (2) rejection sampling (RSO), and (3) KL-regularized reinforcement learning with a relaxation of the marginal KL divergence (KL-Relaxed PPO). We will use the Dall-E dataset and DALL-E model as the pre-trained reference model and fine-tune it for text-to-image generation on the COCO dataset. We will evaluate our approaches using the FID score and Inception score as metrics.
CONTROLS: This experiment includes a baseline where we train the pre-trained DALL-E model from scratch on the COCO dataset and another baseline where we fine-tune the pre-trained model using plain PPO without KL regularization.
COST: 2112.665
PREDICTION: We expect KL-Relaxed PPO to perform better than KL-regularized PPO due to the relaxation of the marginal KL divergence, but worse than rejection sampling due to its lack of robustness to rare samples. Unfortunately, KL-regularized PPO might suffer from unstable training and poor convergence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging KL-Regularization for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We design an experiment where we compare the performance of three fine-tuning approaches for diffusion models: (1) KL-regularized reinforcement learning (PPO), (2) rejection sampling (RSO), and (3) KL-regularized reinforcement learning with a relaxation of the marginal KL divergence (KL-Relaxed PPO). We will use the Dall-E dataset and DALL-E model as the pre-trained reference model and fine-tune it for text-to-image generation on the COCO dataset. We will evaluate our approaches using the FID score and Inception score as metrics.
CONTROLS: This experiment includes a baseline where we train the pre-trained DALL-E model from scratch on the COCO dataset and another baseline where we fine-tune the pre-trained model using plain PPO without KL regularization.
COST: 6400
PREDICTION: We expect KL-Relaxed PPO to perform better than KL-regularized PPO due to the relaxation of the marginal KL divergence, but worse than rejection sampling due to its lack of robustness to rare samples. Unfortunately, KL-regularized PPO might suffer from unstable training and poor convergence.

PREDICTION: We expect rejection sampling to correct the errors of the pre-trained flow model due to discretization error and statistical error of imperfect learning, leading to improved sample quality at a reasonable cost in generation compute.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploiting Multi-Step Generation Structure for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Propose a new fine-tuning method that exploits the multi-step generation structure of diffusion models to regularize the KL divergence between the fine-tuned distribution and the pre-trained model distribution. Specifically, this method uses a penalty term that involves the trajectory-wise KL divergence between entire denoising processes and the corresponding reverse denoising processes. Evaluate this method on the same set of text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation tasks, using the FID and mode-covering score as metrics.
CONTROLS: Trajectory KL-regularized method (proposed), trajectory KL-regularized method with learned trajectory weights, KL term ignored (baseline).
COST: 192000
PREDICTION: The proposed method may alleviate the initial value function bias problem, but could suffer from high instability and mode collapse due to the added complexity. 

This proposal aims to find a more effective strategy to exploit the structure of diffusion and flow models, following the open question on leveraging their structure for making fine-tuning more effective.

TITLE: Investigating Reward-Free Fine-Tuning of Pre-Trained Flow Models using Denoising Percentile Correction
PROPOSAL: Propose a reward-free fine-tuning method for pre-trained flow models based on denoising percentile correction (DPC). DPC leverages the discrepancy between the percentiles of the pre-trained model's denoising distribution and the target data distribution to correct errors in the pre-trained model without explicit rewards. The method is evaluated on text-to-image generation and molecule generation tasks, using metrics such as Inception Score (IS) and FID.
CONTROLS: Adaptation via KL regularization with fixed learned noise schedule, leaving out DPC component (ablation), Training without any adaptation (direct estimation).
COST: 432000
PREDICTION: Although this method might struggle with pre-trained models having high discrepancy and vanishing corrections, the provided correction estimates likely reflect the error of the model in real-time for the considered task domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Iterative Denoising Truncation Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel fine-tuning strategy, Iterative Denoising Truncation (IDT), that adaptively truncates the denoising process as training progresses. At each iteration, we observe the dynamics of the KL divergence between the fine-tuned distribution and the pre-trained model, and stop shortening the denoising trajectory when the KL begins to increase, indicating that further regularization would deteriorate the model's ability to capture the reward. In the alternative (when increasing KL is acceptable for a while at no extra infoentropy cost e.g. first Kl iterations), let the putative most recently-trained signalling mode that KL complies be used with the standard PPO constant step (MSCS), modelling rates convergence before deciding to truncate. This method leverages the multi-step generative structure of diffusion models and allows for effective KL regularization in the presence of intractable marginal likelihoods.
CONTROLS: We compare IDT with standard PPO (without KL regularization) and ProPR (which uses a fixed KL regularization for the entire trajectory).
COST: 20
PREDICTION: IDT outperforms the baseline methods in terms of convergence speed and sample quality, especially in the presence of large errors between the reference distribution and the target data distribution. However, we expect it to fail in settings where the reward function has a long horizon, making it difficult to identify when to truncate the denoising process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Denoising Trajectory gewek Sampling
PROPOSAL: We introduce Denoising Trajectory gewek Sampling (DTgS), a novel sampling method designed to estimate the marginal KL divergence between the fine-tuned distribution and the reference model without requiring access to the marginal likelihood. DTgS leverages the sequential structure of the denoising process and uses an importance-weighted manner to approximate the marginal distribution of the data-generating process. Specifically, we first sample the intermediate denoised states and then use importance sampling to estimate the likelihood of the data given these states. This approximation allows us to regularize the expected reward function using the estimated marginal KL divergence.
CONTROLS: We compare DTgS with standard PPO (without KL regularization), DT-SKC (using a soft KL constraint that averages over the intermediate denoising states), and a naive importance sampling approach without KL regularization.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: DTgS offers a significant improvement over standard PPO in terms of sample quality and convergence speed, especially in regimes where the marginal likelihood is difficult to compute. However, we anticipate it will fail in situations where the intermediate denoising states are highly correlated, leading to biased importance sampling estimates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rejection Sampling for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization
PROPOSAL: We introduce a rejection sampling approach, named ARGOS, designed to fine-tune diffusion models while maintaining KL-regularization. ARGOS incorporates a learned thresholding mechanism to probe the KL gap between the fine-tuned distribution and the reference model and uses importance-weighted sampling to maintain KL regularization while selecting high-reward samples for training. Specifically, ARGOS learns to associate high-reward samples and low-regularization KL-divergence, while retaining full-access to the pre-trained model.
CONTROLS: We compare ARGOS with standard PPO (without KL regularization), IDT, and DTgS.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: ARGOS outperforms the baseline methods and shows competitive results with IDT and DTgS, especially in multimodal settings where maintaining KL regularization is crucial. However, the high computational cost of ARGOS may be a limiting factor in large-scale settings, where the objective function requires multiple evaluations of the expensive reward function and marginal KL divergence estimations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Best-of-N Sampling for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a Best-of-N (BoN) sampling framework, designed to be compatible with KL-regularization in diffusion models. BoN selects high-reward samples based on their pre-trained model log-likelihood, thereby controlling the KL gap between the fine-tuned distribution and the reference model. Specifically, BoN samples multiple iterations of the diffusion process and selects the top-N samples with the highest pre-trained model log-likelihood for training, and KL regularization is maintained by doing one approximation using trajectory estimates.
CONTROLS: We compare BoN with standard PPO (without KL regularization), IDT, DTgS, and ARGOS.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: BoN outperforms the baseline methods, especially in regimes where pre-trained model log-likelihood is a good proxy for reward. However, the performance of BoN may suffer when the reward is very biased or noisy, and using N that is too large may lead to overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Accelerating KL-Regularized Reward Maximization using Few-Shot Imitation Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a few-shot imitation learning approach to accelerate KL-regularized reward maximization in diffusion models. Our method, named KL-FSI, leverages a few expert demonstrations to train a student model that can mimic the expert's behavior while maintaining KL regularization. Specifically, KL-FSI samples a batch of expert demonstrations and uses importance-weighted sampling to learn a student model that generalizes to new samples.
CONTROLS: We compare KL-FSI with standard PPO (without KL regularization), IDT, DTgS, ARGOS, and BoN.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: KL-FSI outperforms the baseline methods, especially in regimes where the reward is difficult to train directly. However, the performance of KL-FSI may suffer when the few-shot demonstrations are not representative of the full reward space, and collecting such expert demonstrations may require significant resources.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for KL-Regularized Reward Maximization in Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-task learning approach to improve KL-regularized reward maximization in diffusion models. Our method, named MT-Diff, leverages a shared representation across multiple reward functions and a KL-regularized objective to learn a more robust and generalizable model. Specifically, MT-Diff trains a model to predict multiple reward functions jointly and maintains KL regularization using a shared denoising process.
CONTROLS: We compare MT-Diff with standard PPO (without KL regularization), IDT, DTgS, ARGOS, BoN, and KL-FSI.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: MT-Diff outperforms the baseline methods, especially in regimes where multiple reward functions are relevant and the model needs to adapt to changing objectives. However, the performance of MT-Diff may suffer when the reward functions are highly diverse or have conflicting objectives.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off in KL-Regularized Reward Maximization using Thompson Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a new approach to the exploration-exploitation trade-off in KL-regularized reward maximization using Thompson sampling. Our method, named T-KL, leverages a probabilistic model to balance exploration and exploitation and maintains KL regularization using a probabilistic denoising process. Specifically, T-KL uses a Bayesian neural network to predict the reward function and samples a new denoising process at each iteration to balance exploration and exploitation.
CONTROLS: We compare T-KL with standard PPO (without KL regularization), IDT, DTgS, ARGOS, BoN, KL-FSI, and MT-Diff.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: T-KL outperforms the baseline methods, especially in regimes where the reward function is unknown and needs to be explored efficiently. However, the performance of T-KL may suffer when the exploration is too aggressive, leading to increased variance in the results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Autoregressive Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning without KL Divergence
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method for fine-tuning diffusion models without using KL divergence regularization. Our approach, named AutoDark, combines autoregressive models with diffusion models to perform fine-tuning. Specifically, AutoDark uses an autoregressive model to predict the next step in the diffusion process and maintains a fixed denoising schedule. We demonstrate that AutoDark outperforms KL-regularized methods in certain scenarios and provides a new perspective on fine-tuning diffusion models.
CONTROLS: We compare AutoDark with standard PPO (without KL regularization), IDT, DTgS, ARGOS, BoN, KL-FSI, MT-Diff, and T-KL.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: AutoDark offers a promising alternative for fine-tuning diffusion models and can outperform KL-regularized methods in certain regimes. However, the performance of AutoDark may suffer when the autoregressive model is not well-calibrated or when the diffusion process is too complex.

TITLE: Investigating the Effects of RMS Normalization on Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: We design an experiment to study how RMS normalization impacts the behavior of activation steering techniques, specifically activation addition and directional ablation, on a real-world LLM using a dataset of human-written text. We measure the effectiveness of steering in inducing the desired behavior while preserving model coherence using a combination of automated metrics (e.g., fluency and factuality) and human evaluation (assessed using an annotate task). 
CONTROLS: This experiment is compared to a baseline where RMS normalization is disabled. We also test the steering techniques with a standard RMS normalization scale.
COST: 21126.65
PREDICTION: The results will show that modifying the RMS normalization scale significantly affects the behavior of the steering techniques, and a fixed normalization scale might not be ideal for a wide range of requests since the effects of addition and ablation can slightly vary across contexts and models. However, a scaling normalization approach can mitigate some of these issues, reducing degradation in model fluency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-Specific Scaling for Activation Addition
PROPOSAL: We explore the feasibility of using a coefficient that scales output depending on the activation norm of each layer for activation addition. By using this approach, we find the scaling relationship between the coefficient and the activation norm for each layer, so the scaling between layers can effectively be made more comparable and the search for optimal coefficients can become less brittle. We will evaluate this method by applying it to our previous experiment setup, where we use the RMS normalization-modified model, and test its effectiveness in controlling the model's refusal of harmful requests while maintaining model coherence.
CONTROLS: We compare this layer-specific scaling approach against standard activation addition and against an ablation study where we systematically vary the scaling between layers.
COST: 24300
PREDICTION: The introduction of layer-specific scaling for activation addition should provide more consistent and robust performance across different model layers and reduce its brittleness. However, the expected gains may vary depending on model architecture, and it's not certain how well this will generalize across task types.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Directional Projection for Orthogonalized Ablation
PROPOSAL: As a method for more selective editing of the model activations, we propose an alternative to orthogonalized ablation that selects the direction in which to ablate the activations based on a learned objective, rather than relying on the contrastive examples. We design a learnable directional projection head that maps the activations to a lower-dimensional representation and is optimized during a validation phase to produce a specific target desired behavior. By using this projection, we can perform more targeted ablation of the activations along the learned directions, improving the approach's effectiveness and selectivity.
CONTROLS: We compare this method to standard orthogonalized ablation and to a study where we apply orthogonalized ablation with varying numbers of selected directions to evaluate its robustness and efficacy in maintaining the desired behavior.
COST: 38073
PREDICTION: This approach should significantly improve the effectiveness and selectivity of orthogonalized ablation by adaptively learning which directions to ablate, potentially offering a more robust and targeted solution for behavioral control in LLMs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Emotional Expression Control with Steering
PROPOSAL: Given that existing steering methods may not provide fine-grained control over the generation of text with specific emotional tone, we propose an experiment where we apply and evaluate various steering methods to control the emotional expression of generated text. We select a well-known dataset for Emotion Recognition In Conversations (ERC) and follow the typical procedure for data preparation, and test various steering techniques for their effectiveness in inducing and suppressing specific emotions in text generation.
CONTROLS: This study is compared to a baseline where no steering is applied. We also test the relativity of the steering methods to different emotional tone generation tasks with varying severity and subtlety.
COST: 62000
PREDICTION: Steering for emotional expression control is a complex task, but with the introduction of directional projection for orthogonalized ablation and layer-specific scaling for activation addition, we should see better performance in steering the model's emotional tone. However, hitting a precise tone can be challenging due to the subjective nature of emotional expression, and the model may struggle to produce nuanced emotional effects.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing Interference Between Behavioral Control and Language Modeling
PROPOSAL: To evaluate how steering techniques impact the model's broader behavioral capacity and generalizability, we propose an experiment where we measure the effects of various steering methods on language modeling performance. We assess how different levels of steering strength (e.g., adding or ablating specific behaviors) affect the model's ability to generate coherent and grammatically correct text on a separate language modeling task. This investigation can help us understand whether steering is a zero-sum game, where improvements in behavior control come at a cost to language modeling performance.
CONTROLS: This study is compared to a baseline where no steering is applied. We also test how different steering methods and their strengths affect language modeling performance to evaluate their relative impact.
COST: 76000
PREDICTION: If steering effectively controls specific behaviors without compromising language modeling performance, we should observe minimal to no decline in the model's ability to generate natural and coherent text on a separate task. However, if steering comes at a cost, we expect to see performance degradation with increased steering strength.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning Situational Context for Steerable Controls
PROPOSAL: We explore the possibility of designing steerable controls that are conditional on the environmental context, leveraging relevance estimates or contextual embeddings to cue the steering mechanism. This enables more flexible and nuanced control over behavioral aspects of LLM outputs. We incorporate contextual information into steering through learned attention mechanisms that condition the steering onto contextual representations. By evaluating this contextualized approach, we aim to demonstrate improved adaptability and generalization of steering controls across diverse scenarios.
CONTROLS: We compare the contextualized steering approach to traditional non-contextual approaches and also conduct an ablation study to assess the significance of contextual embedding in steering control.
COST: 106832.2
PREDICTION: The incorporation of situational context will likely provide more flexibility and robustness to steering controls, improving their ability to steer away from objectionable content or respond more cogently to emotionally charged queries.

TITLE: Investigating Activation Steering with Positional Weighting
PROPOSAL: We propose an extension to directional ablation by incorporating positional weighting, allowing the model to selectively interact with different activations at various depth levels when controlling for specific behaviors. Specifically, we will modify the orthogonal projection in directional ablation to be position-dependent.
CONTROLS: We will compare against the original directional ablation method, as well as activation addition with layer-wise coefficients, and report the performance of these baselines on a set of curated real-world benchmarks for refusal of harmful requests and emotion control of generated text.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: By allowing for positional weighting, this extension has the potential to mitigate the limitation of unabated feature suppression, as it gives the model more flexibility to fine-tune the depth level at which a behavior is controlled, but we might encounter brittleness due to the need for precise position weighting coefficients.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Quantifying Activation Steering in Normalized Activation Spaces
PROPOSAL: Given the widespread adoption of RMS normalization in contemporary LLMs, we investigate how existing activation steering operations behave and interact with each other when applied to normalized activations. We will derive a theoretical framework for understanding the effects of normalization on activation steering, and experimentally validate our findings on multiple LLMs across various sizes.
CONTROLS: We will compare our findings against baseline models that do not apply RMS normalization, as well as against the original activation steering operations without positional weighting (from proposal 1).

PREDICTION: By understanding how normalization affects activation steering, we can develop more effective steering methods, but our analysis might reveal inherent limitations of current steering operations due to normalization, requiring a radical departure from existing approaches.

PREDICTION: We expect to see limited effectiveness of current activation steering methods in suppressing highly abstract or context-dependent behaviors, such as emotion control, and possibly disrupted fluency or coherence when attempting to refuse/allow specific requests.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring Activation Rotation Prone to Misalignment
PROPOSAL: We analyze the orthogonalization process used in directional ablation, specifically the phenomenon where activation rotation leads to feature misalignment. We search for pairs of feature vectors in the activation space of a language model, where orthogonalization unintentionally aligns them, causing behavior instability and loss of coherent outputs. We then use domain knowledge and contrastive examples to validate our results and explore how model normalization influences this effect.
CONTROLS: Examine model variations before and after RMS normalization and analyze its impact on feature misalignment in the activation space.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The activation rotation prone to misalignment often arises in deeper layers and is more frequent when the input data is less controlled or of low quality.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Activation Projection with Optimal Perturbation for Behavior Steering
PROPOSAL: We introduce a variant of directional ablation, called Optimal Perturbation Abstraction (OPA), to steer LLMs towards specific behaviors. OPA minimizes the perturbation magnitude needed to project the activation onto the orthogonal complement of a target feature direction, which ensures fine-grained control and reduces potential behavioral degradation. We evaluate OPA on a range of behavior control tasks and compare its performance to existing steering techniques.
CONTROLS: Compare against current methods of additivity, ablation, and conditional methods.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: OPA achieves more consistent results in steering towards specific behaviors, especially when controlling positive requests, compared to existing approaches, due to its optimal perturbation nature. However, its performance may degrade in noisy or low-quality input data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuously Controlled Activation Steering (CCAS)
PROPOSAL: Implement a resonator mechanism that modifies the activation space of a pre-trained transformer-based language model by smoothly scaling the component of the hidden state along a target behavior's feature direction. This is done by computing an exponential moving average (EMA) of the target behavior's feature vector, which controls the amount of influence the feature has on the model's outputs. The EMA's decay rate is the control parameter, allowing for continuous, fine-grained control over the expression of the target behavior. The model is trained only once to obtain a good initialization of the feature direction, and can be applied to various downstream tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare to directional ablation (orthogonalization) and activation addition, using datasets like HOTDOG and ORIG_T3, and metrics such as quality, coherence, and refusal rates. Investigate the impact of the decay rate on the steering quality.
COST: 2304
PREDICTION: CCAS should provide more nuanced control over the target behavior, outperforming directional ablation in most scenarios. However, the choice of decay rate may become critical, and incorrect settings could lead to degraded performance or incoherent outputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Heterogeneous Federated Multi-task Learning without Model Congruity
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of the state-of-the-art federated multi-task learning method, Federated Multi-task Learning with Model-based Knowledge Distillation (i.e., [22] with an added knowledge distillation term), with a new method, Federated Multi-task Learning with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Specifically, each user's fine-tuned foundation model will be converted into a node in a heterogeneous graph, where edges will be built based on the similarity between their task-specific predictors. A GNN will then learn to aggregate representations of all users, and finally, a downstream task-specific predictor will be trained on each node's representation. Different users can have distinct architecture sizes and numbers of layers.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be the state-of-the-art federated multi-task learning method without the added knowledge distillation term, and ablations will evaluate the contributions of different components in the proposed model.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The proposed method with GNN is expected to perform better than the baseline and the Federated Multi-task Learning with Model-based Knowledge Distillation method, especially in tasks with significantly different data distributions. The proposed method might fail if there is a large class imbalance among tasks, as the GNN might perform poorly in such scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adjustable Federated Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop an adjustable federated contrastive learning (AFL) method that can balance the number of negative pairs for each positive pair in a data-efficient manner. AFL will use a mutual information estimator as a proxy measure to dynamically adjust local margins in the InfoNCE loss, ensuring that a sufficient number of negative pairs are collected to avoid the collapse of the shared representation space. AFL will also utilize a learned temporal dependency to capture long-term knowledge transfer across all users and model variants.
CONTROLS: AFL's performance will be compared against original InfoNCE, and the state-of-the-art ALI (Adversarial Lightweight Information) loss with adjustments for across multiple users and modalities, using Task A, Task B and the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets in federated settings; and ablations will be evaluated to understand the impact of adjusting the margin and the learned temporal dependency on the overall performance.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: AFL is expected to outperform the baselines, especially in the regime where a moderate number of shared parameters is desired, and will likely fail when the server-side communication is extremely limited, making it harder to achieve efficient knowledge transfer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Grammar-based Collaborative Federated Learning (GCF)
PROPOSAL: Introduce Grammar-based Collaborative Federated Learning (GCF), which leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) and a graph attention mechanism to capture interactions between users' task-specific representations. The grammar is constructed by aligning the task-agnostic components (_FAST!) of the user models, rather than their task-specific components. A GNN then propagates information across the task-agnostic space, capturing holistic interactions across users with heterogenous tasks.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be the original Federated Learning (FL) framework with a graph neural network (GNN) attempting to capture complex interactions; evaluations will also be made of AGL (Augmented Grammar Loss) to benchmark its efficiency and performance; the original AFL will also be compared with varying settings.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: The proposed GCF is expected to capture a richer set of holistic interactions between user models, improving knowledge sharing and collaborative learning, but its performance may suffer if any user's task-specific tasks is a dominant component of its overall embedding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Heterogeneous Federated Multi-task Learning without Model Congruity
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of the state-of-the-art federated multi-task learning method, Federated Multi-task Learning with Model-based Knowledge Distillation (i.e., [22] with an added knowledge distillation term), with a new method, Federated Multi-task Learning with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Specifically, each user's fine-tuned foundation model will be converted into a node in a heterogeneous graph, where edges will be built based on the similarity between their task-specific predictors. A GNN will then learn to aggregate representations of all users, and finally, a downstream task-specific predictor will be trained on each node's representation. Different users can have distinct architecture sizes and numbers of layers.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be the state-of-the-art federated multi-task learning method without the added knowledge distillation term, and ablations will evaluate the contributions of different components in the proposed model.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: The proposed method with GNN is expected to perform better than the baseline and the Federated Multi-task Learning with Model-based Knowledge Distillation method, especially in tasks with significantly different data distributions. The proposed method might fail if there is a large class imbalance among tasks, as the GNN might perform poorly in such scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adjustable Federated Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop an adjustable federated contrastive learning (AFL) method that can balance the number of negative pairs for each positive pair in a data-efficient manner. AFL will use a mutual information estimator as a proxy measure to dynamically adjust local margins in the InfoNCE loss, ensuring that a sufficient number of negative pairs are collected to avoid the collapse of the shared representation space. AFL will also utilize a learned temporal dependency to capture long-term knowledge transfer across all users and model variants.
CONTROLS: AFL's performance will be compared against original InfoNCE, and the state-of-the-art ALI (Adversarial Lightweight Information) loss with adjustments for across multiple users and modalities, using Task A, Task B and the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets in federated settings; and ablations will be evaluated to understand the impact of adjusting the margin and the learned temporal dependency on the overall performance.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: AFL is expected to outperform the baselines, especially in the regime where a moderate number of shared parameters is desired, and will likely fail when the server-side communication is extremely limited, making it harder to achieve efficient knowledge transfer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Grammar-based Collaborative Federated Learning (GCF)
PROPOSAL: Introduce Grammar-based Collaborative Federated Learning (GCF), which leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) and a graph attention mechanism to capture interactions between users' task-specific representations. The grammar is constructed by aligning the task-agnostic components (_FAST!) of the user models, rather than their task-specific components. A GNN then propagates information across the task-agnostic space, capturing holistic interactions across users with heterogenous tasks.
CONTROLS: The baseline will be the original Federated Learning (FL) framework with a graph neural network (GNN) attempting to capture complex interactions; evaluations will also be made of AGL (Augmented Grammar Loss) to benchmark its efficiency and performance; the original AFL will also be compared with varying settings.
COST: 14400
PREDICTION: The proposed GCF is expected to capture a richer set of holistic interactions between user models, improving knowledge sharing and collaborative learning, but its performance may suffer if any user's task-specific tasks is a dominant component of its overall embedding.

ACTION: REVISE

We will leverage a learned factor (factor ensemble) for each user to learn a personalized weight and balance filter constraint for their task.
CONTROLS: Compared to the state-of-the-art method AFL for federated knowledge sharing in multi-modal, multi-task scenarios on FEMNIST, WikiText2 & ImageCLEF datasets.

PREDICTION: AFL+ is expected to achieve better performance compared to AFL especially in balance across tasks and alleviate imbalance by itself, which is necessary in real scenarios but still could be difficult if it's extremely difficult with tasks specialization, like CNN-based processes and easier processes.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Federated Multi-task Learning with Joint Alignment and Communication-Efficient Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel federated multi-task learning framework that addresses task heterogeneity by imposing a shared representation space across models with heterogeneous architectures. We introduce a Gramian-based contrastive loss with an additional regularizer to promote communication efficiency. During local updates, each user's encoder will be updated jointly with the shared representation, which is a transformation of the Gram matrix of the user's representations. To further improve communication efficiency, we use a sampled Softmax loss on the server side, where the temperature is set dynamically based on the number of users and their convergence speed.
CONTROLS: We compare to recent federated multi-task learning methods (e.g., PC at SGC, AdMoC, GT-EG) and ablate the Gramian-based contrastive loss, the regularizer, and the sampled Softmax. We also experiment with knowledge distillation and knowledge-based approaches as baselines.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Our method significantly outperforms baselines, and the Gramian-based contrastive loss and the regularizer are crucial to achieving favorable results. However, the sampled Softmax might not work well with a large number of users, where the temperature would need to be dynamically adjusted to avoid numerical instability.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Representation Learning with Orthogonal Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose an orthogonal transfer scheme that enables users to transfer task-agnostic knowledge across multiple tasks without requiring architectural congruity. Each user maintains a separate set of latent spaces for each task, which are enforced to be maximally orthogonal using a task-agnostic regularization term. This allows for knowledge transfer across tasks without compromising personalization. The server aggregates representations from all users and performs a joint contrastive learning task, aligning the task-agnostic knowledge within the representation space.
CONTROLS: We compare with the previous proposal, removing the Gramian-based contrastive loss and the regularizer, and instead use orthogonal transfer with traditional contrastive learning. We also ablate the task-agnostic regularization term and compare with a method that uses a shared representation space.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Our orthogonal transfer scheme significantly improves over the traditional contrastive learning baseline, especially when the number of tasks is large. However, the task-agnostic regularization term might not be effective when the tasks have a large number of classes, requiring a more complex object-level prior knowledge.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a task-agnostic meta-learning framework for federated multi-task learning. The framework uses a meta-learning objective that trains a parameterized representation function to learn a task-agnostic initialization scheme. During local updates, each user's encoder is trained with a task-specific adaptation mechanism that adapts the task-agnostic initialization to their specific task. This allows users to leverage task-agnostic knowledge without compromising task-specific personalization.
CONTROLS: We compare with the rotated transfer scheme and traditional meta-learning methods. We also experiment with ablations of the task-agnostic initialization and adaptation mechanisms.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Our task-agnostic meta-learning framework outperforms traditional meta-learning methods, especially when the tasks have a large number of classes. However, the effectiveness of the task-agnostic initialization scheme might depend on the specific task distribution and require more complex hyperparameter tuning.

TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Joint Alignment and Adaptive Communication
PROPOSAL: We modify the original joint alignment method to incorporate an adaptive communication mechanism that dynamically allocates the length and frequency of messages transmitted between clients and the server, based on the clients' convergence speed and participating frequency. This allows the framework to adaptively learn from clients that are more likely to be converging, improving overall performance.
CONTROLS: We compare with the original joint alignment method, as well as with a baseline that uses fixed-length and fixed-frequency communication.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Our adaptive communication mechanism significantly improves upon the original joint alignment method, especially in scenarios with heterogeneous clients with varying local data properties. However, the optimal adaptive communication strategy might depend on the specific client learning parameters and require additional hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Minimax Mixed Federated Learning for Secure and Private Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel minimax mixed federated learning framework that integrates the strengths of both concrete and probabilistic uncertainty to achieve both security and privacy in multi-task learning. The framework involves solving a minimax game between a constrained risk minimizer and an adversary, allowing users to achieve desirable performance while maintaining security and privacy.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the framework using metrics that assess both performance and security, and compare it to existing federated learning methods that prioritize either security or performance.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Our minimax mixed federated learning framework achieves improved performance and security compared to existing methods, but may require significant computational resources to achieve convergence. Additionally, the security benefits may come at the cost of increased communication overhead.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Federated Multi-task Learning with Joint Alignment and Communication-Efficient Knowledge Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel federated multi-task learning framework that addresses task heterogeneity by imposing a shared representation space across models with heterogeneous architectures. We introduce a Gramian-based contrastive loss with an additional regularizer to promote communication efficiency. During local updates, each user's encoder will be updated jointly with the shared representation, which is a transformation of the Gram matrix of the user's representations. To further improve communication efficiency, we use a sampled Softmax loss on the server side, where the temperature is set dynamically based on the number of users and their convergence speed.
CONTROLS: We compare to recent federated multi-task learning methods (e.g., PC at SGC, AdMoC, GT-EG) and ablate the Gramian-based contrastive loss, the regularizer, and the sampled Softmax. We also experiment with knowledge distillation and knowledge-based approaches as baselines.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Our method significantly outperforms baselines, and the Gramian-based contrastive loss and the regularizer are crucial to achieving favorable results. However, the sampled Softmax might not work well with a large number of users, where the temperature would need to be dynamically adjusted to avoid numerical instability.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Representation Learning with Orthogonal Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose an orthogonal transfer scheme that enables users to transfer task-agnostic knowledge across multiple tasks without requiring architectural congruity. Each user maintains a separate set of latent spaces for each task, which are enforced to be maximally orthogonal using a task-agnostic regularization term. This allows for knowledge transfer across tasks without compromising personalization. The server aggregates representations from all users and performs a joint contrastive learning task, aligning the task-agnostic knowledge within the representation space.
CONTROLS: We compare with the previous proposal, removing the Gramian-based contrastive loss and the regularizer, and instead use orthogonal transfer with traditional contrastive learning. We also ablate the task-agnostic regularization term and compare with a method that uses a shared representation space.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Our orthogonal transfer scheme significantly improves over the traditional contrastive learning baseline, especially when the number of tasks is large. However, the task-agnostic regularization term might not be effective when the tasks have a large number of classes, requiring a more complex object-level prior knowledge.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Representation Learning with Rotated Transfer
PROPOSAL: We modify the orthogonal transfer scheme by introducing a rotation mechanism that enhances task-agnostic knowledge transfer. The rotation mechanism considers the strength of task-specific information and adaptively adjusts the weights of orthogonal constraints, allowing for a more effective transfer of common knowledge across tasks. The server-side contrastive learning task remains unchanged.
CONTROLS: We compare with the previous version of the orthogonal transfer scheme, as well as with a baseline that does not use task-agnostic transfer. We also ablate the rotation mechanism and experiment with different rotation schedules.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Our rotated transfer scheme significantly outperforms the previous orthogonal transfer scheme, especially when the tasks have a large number of classes or complex object-level prior knowledge. However, the effectiveness of the rotation mechanism might depend on the specific task distribution and require more complex hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a task-agnostic meta-learning framework for federated multi-task learning. The framework uses a meta-learning objective that trains a parameterized representation function to learn a task-agnostic initialization scheme. During local updates, each user's encoder is trained with a task-specific adaptation mechanism that adapts the task-agnostic initialization to their specific task. This allows users to leverage task-agnostic knowledge without compromising task-specific personalization.
CONTROLS: We compare with the rotated transfer scheme and traditional meta-learning methods. We also experiment with ablations of the task-agnostic initialization and adaptation mechanisms.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Our task-agnostic meta-learning framework outperforms traditional meta-learning methods, especially when the tasks have a large number of classes. However, the effectiveness of the task-agnostic initialization scheme might depend on the specific task distribution and require more complex hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Joint Alignment and Adaptive Communication
PROPOSAL: We modify the original joint alignment method to incorporate an adaptive communication mechanism that dynamically allocates the length and frequency of messages transmitted between clients and the server, based on the clients' convergence speed and participating frequency. This allows the framework to adaptively learn from clients that are more likely to be converging, improving overall performance.
CONTROLS: We compare with the original joint alignment method, as well as with a baseline that uses fixed-length and fixed-frequency communication.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Our adaptive communication mechanism significantly improves upon the original joint alignment method, especially in scenarios with heterogeneous clients with varying local data properties. However, the optimal adaptive communication strategy might depend on the specific client learning parameters and require additional hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigating the Efficacy of Federated Multi-Task Learning on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: We conduct a comprehensive investigation of the efficacy of federated multi-task learning on a variety of real-world datasets, including but not limited to climate science, medical imaging, and visual question answering tasks. We evaluate the performance of our existing proposals on these datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art methods that leverage domain adaptation, transfer learning, and knowledge distillation.
CONTROLS: We use the same evaluation metrics across all datasets and compare the results of our existing proposals with those of state-of-the-art methods. We also conduct a number of ablation studies to assess the impact of individual components of our methods.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Our investigation reveals that the efficacy of federated multi-task learning depends on the properties of the datasets and tasks involved. Some of our existing proposals perform well on certain datasets, while others struggle to achieve good results. This suggests that there may be opportunities for further improvements in the field.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Minimax Mixed Federated Learning for Secure and Private Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel minimax mixed federated learning framework that integrates the strengths of both concrete and probabilistic uncertainty to achieve both security and privacy in multi-task learning. The framework involves solving a minimax game between a constrained risk minimizer and an adversary, allowing users to achieve desirable performance while maintaining security and privacy.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the framework using metrics that assess both performance and security, and compare it to existing federated learning methods that prioritize either security or performance.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Our minimax mixed federated learning framework achieves improved performance and security compared to existing methods, but may require significant computational resources to achieve convergence. Additionally, the security benefits may come at the cost of increased communication overhead.

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel federated multi-task learning framework that utilizes a hypergraph structured representation to capture complex interactions between multiple tasks and users. PREDICTION: Our framework achieves improved performance and scalability compared to existing methods, but may require significant computational resources to build and maintain the hypergraph structure. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Model Agnostic Contrastive Loss
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel federated multi-task learning algorithm that combines a model-agnostic contrastive loss with a proximal term based on centered kernel alignment. This loss function is designed to align representations from multiple models with arbitrary architectures and tasks, promoting knowledge transfer without requiring model congruity. We will experiment on a federation of 5 users with different model architectures and tasks (image classification, object detection, sentiment analysis), using a dataset composed of 10% public, 90% private data for each user.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to two baselines: (1) a federated multi-task learning algorithm assuming model congruity, and (2) a model-agnostic federated learning algorithm that transfers knowledge through a shared representation space but lacks the contrastive loss component.
COST: 2880
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed algorithm to outperform the baselines in terms of task accuracy, especially when the number of users increases and public data becomes scarce. Potentially, the model-agnostic contrastive loss will help capture dependencies among representations from different models, promoting task-agnostic information sharing. However, if the proximal term dominates the loss function, model convergence might be slowed down due to high computational complexity.

TITLE: Federated Representation Learning with Multiresolution Granularity
PROPOSAL: We propose a federated representation learning framework that adaptively adjusts the granularity of representation alignment based on the resolution of the input data. Specifically, we assign different numbers of convolutional and fully connected layers to hash the representations at multiple resolutions. This approach facilitates the alignment of representations from models with varying architectures and input dimensions (e.g., images, text, audio). We will experiment on a federation of users with image classification, object detection, and speech recognition tasks, using datasets such as CIFAR-10, COCO, and LibriSpeech.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to existing federated multi-task learning methods that assume model congruity or apply a fixed resolution for representation alignment.
COST: 8640
PREDICTION: We expect the multiresolution granularity framework to improve representation alignment and knowledge transfer among users with diverse tasks and input dimensions. However, if the resolution of the input data varies significantly across tasks, fine-tuning the granularity threshold might become a challenging and computationally expensive hyperparameter tuning process.

TITLE: Federated Semi-Supervised Learning with Cross-Modal Alignment
PROPOSAL: We propose a federated semi-supervised learning algorithm that combines cross-modal alignment and pseudo-labeling techniques to capture both local and shared information across users with different tasks and modalities (e.g., text-image, speech-image). Our approach uses a graph neural network to align representations from different modalities and constructs a pseudo-labeling graph to relax the scarcity of supervised labels. We will experiment on a federation of users with image captioning, object detection, and sentiment analysis tasks, using the COCO dataset.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to existing federated semi-supervised learning methods that rely on pairwise alignment or task-specific pseudo-labeling.
COST: 15295
PREDICTION: We expect the cross-modal alignment framework to improve pseudo-labeling accuracy and representation alignment across users with different modalities. However, if the modalities are highly dissimilar, the graph neural network might struggle to learn meaningful alignments, leading to suboptimal performance.

TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Arbitrary Architectures and Tasks
PROPOSAL:  Experiment with Federated Fat-Tail Neural Tarbell (FFτNt) algorithm, a novel method that creates a shared, latent-space embedding for users' representations across multiple tasks and arbitrarily different architectures. Each user computes its task-specific predictor and a task-agnostic embedding, which is then aligned with the corresponding embeddings from other users via a carefully designed InfoNCE loss variant.
CONTROLS:  Compare against recent methods for federated multi-task learning, such as the shared-encoder approach and knowledge-distillation-based methods, on 3 real-world benchmarks (FedEMNIST, ShiDianNiu, and SQuAD).
COST: 121000
PREDICTION:  FFτNt improves overall accuracy and convergence speed, especially in scenarios with diverse tasks and user architectures. Its effectiveness may be hampered by the relatively high computation required for building task-agnostic embeddings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Global Representation Alignment via Orthogonal Procrustes
PROPOSAL:  Investigate the use of Orthogonal Procrustes to align the task-agnostic representations obtained by the previous FFτNt algorithm across all users, leveraging its mathematical guarantee for retaining information and preserving alignment. This orthogonal alignment should enhance the quality of shared representations and, consequently, the knowledge transfer across diverse models.
CONTROLS:  Relax the orthogonal constraint to empirically measure the effect of losing orthogonality on the overall performance.
COST:  240960
PREDICTION:  Orthogonal Procrustes significantly improves knowledge transfer, collaboration robustness, and, on average, lifts the overall accuracy compared to FFτNt. Practical implementation may require more careful optimization due to orthogonality constraints.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Global Representation Alignment via Orthogonal Procrustes, with Proximal Regularization
PROPOSAL:  Rethink using Orthogonal Procrustes directly on task-agnostic representations from FFτNt, which may not necessarily lead to orthogonality. Instead, propose using a proximal term that encourages all task-agnostic representations to become orthonormal vectors, reflecting the similarities across users' locally learned data while not strictly requiring exact representation matching. This adaptability may improve convergence rates and reduce the risk of representation degeneration.
CONTROLS:  Compare the revised approach with standard orthogonal Procrustes (ortholithic variant) and a naive all-zero initialization baseline on high heterogeneity scenarios.
COST:  275000
PREDICTION:  Adapting to Procrustes optimization through the task-agnostic representations leads to better convergence and accuracy overall, treating task heterogeneity effectively. Some specific user settings might reveal a decreased performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Knowledge Transfer via Transferable Augmentations
PROPOSAL:  Introduce transferable augmentations, specifically developed to capture common, task-agnostic information across diverse architectural and task settings, to augment the input data fed to the task-specific predictors. As transferable augmentations are trained solely on the task-agnostic representations, they allow for sharing and consolidation of common knowledge across multiple tasks without requiring exact architectural congruity.
CONTROLS:  Compare transferable augmentations with popular augmentation methods (e.g., DropOut, Flipping) on FedEMNIST, ShiDianNiu, and SQuAD, examining their impact on knowledge transfer, collaboration efficiency, and model accuracy.
COST:  580000
PREDICTION:  Transferable augmentations significantly enhance knowledge transfer while allowing for optional use in conjunction with FFτNt, although their effectiveness might vary based on user-specifications and task requirements.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable Knowledge Distillation for Heterogeneous Architectures
PROPOSAL:  Propose a knowledge distillation framework tailored specifically to the multi-task setting with heterogeneous architectures. By leveraging task-agnostic representations and knowledge transfer through transferable augmentations, this method is capable of sharing distilled knowledge across users with diverse models without calculating loss functions on the target architectures directly.
CONTROLS:  Compare the proposed knowledge distillation framework with naive knowledge distillation methods on learning-specific variants of FFτNt's task-agnostic representations, evaluating its efficiency in aligning diverse user models on several task combinations.
COST:  864000
PREDICTION:  This scalable knowledge distillation framework will effectively speed up knowledge transfer across various architectures and tasks, outperforming naive approaches by reducing model differences.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Arbitrary Architectures and Tasks, Using Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL:  Refine the initial FFτNt algorithm by incorporating knowledge distillation as a supplementary mechanism for knowledge transfer. Specifically, distill task-agnostic representations from strong models into weak ones, leveraging the scalable distillation framework to enhance collaboration between diverse user models while preserving their unique capabilities.
CONTROLS:  Compare the revised FFτNt with its original counterpart, the previously proposed scalable distillation framework, on a range of challenging scenarios (e.g., cross-task transfer).
COST:  1260000
PREDICTION:  This revised FFτNt exhibits improved robustness and adaptability through hybrid learning (federated multi-task learning with knowledge distillation), leading to higher collaboration efficiency and generally enhanced performance across various user settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Graph-Based Representation Optimization for Heterogeneous Models
PROPOSAL:  Develop a graph-based optimization framework to incorporate both task-agnostic and task-specific relationships among diverse user models in a collaborative multi-task learning setting. By constructing a joint representation graph, model interactions are explored and optimally transferred through dynamic message passing, leveraging orthogonality regularization to refine the alignments across models.
CONTROLS:  Investigate on a specially designed synthetic benchmark accounting for architectural heterogeneity, comparing with the baseline FFτNt frameworks (Dist and N-Dist).
COST:  1900000
PREDICTION:  The joint graph-based optimization framework improves overall collaboration efficiency, successfully bridging model disparities, and consistently unless when the models are structurally mutually incoherent.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Heterogeneous Models under Model Incongruity
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel federated multi-task learning framework, " FedMatch ", that allows users with heterogeneous model architectures and different tasks to collaboratively improve their customized models without the need for architectural congruity. FedMatch uses a match-based ensemble approach, where each user's model is matched with a subset of other models that are most relevant to its task and architecture.
CONTROLS: We will compare FedMatch with state-of-the-art methods such as FedProx, FedProgD, and match-based methods that assume model congruity.
COST: 1068.322
PREDICTION: FedMatch is expected to outperform the baseline methods, particularly in tasks with limited user participation, due to its ability to match models based on relevance to the task and architecture. However, it may fail in extreme cases where there is a large mismatch between user models and tasks.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Gramian-Based Contrastive Learning for Joint Representation Alignment
PROPOSAL: We propose a Gramian-based contrastive learning algorithm, " GramSync ", that aligns representations from an arbitrary number of models jointly, capturing the dependencies among all of them. This approach builds upon recent work in Gramian-based contrastive learning and extends it to the federated multi-task setting.
CONTROLS: We will compare GramSync with pairwise contrastive learning methods such as InfoNCE and GramSync with knowledge distillation-based methods as ablations.
COST: 1734.5
PREDICATION: GramSync is expected to outperform pairwise contrastive learning methods, especially in settings with a large number of models, due to its ability to capture multi-model dependencies. However, its performance may degrade in tasks with noisy or low-quality data.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Practical Evaluation on Multi-Modal Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a comprehensive, practical evaluation framework for multi-modal federated learning, focusing on the challenges of aligning different modalities such as images and text. We will implement a set of established and recent state-of-the-art methods, including FedMatch and GramSync, in a real-world scenario where federated learning is integrated with a large-scale data sharing platform.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the methods using a combination of multi-modal datasets (e.g., COCO and LISA-VOT) and real-world applications (e.g., visual question answering and image captioning).
COST: 2112.665
PREDICTION: Our experimental results are expected to demonstrate the effectiveness of FedMatch and GramSync in handling multi-modal data and provide valuable insights into practical federated learning scenarios. However, we might encounter difficulties in achieving state-of-the-art performance on very large-scale data due to compute and communication limitations.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Federated Learning with Adversarial Training
PROPOSAL: We propose an adversarial training approach for model-agnostic federated learning, " FedAdv ", which can be integrated with existing federated learning methods such as FedMatch and GramSync. FedAdv uses a discriminator to adversarially train the models on the shared feature space to ensure that the learned representations are robust and invariant to different model architectures and tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare FedAdv with state-of-the-art methods for model-agnostic federated learning, such as those using centered kernel alignment.
COST: 2531.2
PREDICTION: FedAdv is expected to enhance the robustness and transferability of the learned representations, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks. However, its performance may be sensitive to the choice of hyperparameters, particularly when dealing with diverse model architectures and tasks.

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel federated multi-task learning framework, " FedMatch ", that allows users with heterogeneous model architectures and different tasks to collaboratively improve their customized models without the need for architectural congruity. FedMatch uses a match-based ensemble approach, where each user's model is matched with a subset of other models that are most relevant to its task and architecture.
CONTROLS: We will compare FedMatch with state-of-the-art methods such as FedProx, FedProgD, and match-based methods that assume model congruity.

TITLE: Gramian-Based Contrastive Learning for Joint Representation Alignment
PROPOSAL: We propose a Gramian-based contrastive learning algorithm, " GramSync ", that aligns representations from an arbitrary number of models jointly, capturing the dependencies among all of them. This approach builds upon recent work in Gramian-based contrastive learning and extends it to the federated multi-task setting.
CONTROLS: We will compare GramSync with pairwise contrastive learning methods such as InfoNCE and GramSync with knowledge distillation-based methods as ablations.
COST: 5200
PREDICATION: GramSync is expected to outperform pairwise contrastive learning methods, especially in settings with a large number of models, due to its ability to capture multi-model dependencies. However, its performance may degrade in tasks with noisy or low-quality data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Instance-Dependent Label Noise with Two-Stage Model Selection
PROPOSAL: We will implement a novel two-stage model selection approach that combines the strengths of existing methods for handling instance-dependent label noise. In the first stage, we will use the FilteredSemiSupervised method to select clean samples and update the model based on a combination of both the noisy and clean samples. In the second stage, we will use the cluster-based iterative refinement (CBIR) method to identify clusters of samples with similar error patterns and refine the labels on those samples based on their predicted confidence levels. We will test our method on the WWII through GD dataset and compare it to existing state-of-the-art methods, such as LeCun, Noise Correcting Autoencoders and Co-teaching.
CONTROLS: LeCun, Noise Correcting Autoencoders and Co-teaching
COST: 18900
PREDICTION: We expect our two-stage model selection approach to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods in handling instance-dependent label noise, particularly in the second stage. However, our method may fail if we are unable to effectively identify clusters of samples with similar error patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Performance of a Confidence-Based Sample Selection Method
PROPOSAL: We will implement a confidence-based sample selection method that leverages the output of a neural network to identify confident predictions and isolates samples with low confidence as suspected noisy instances. This method will utilize the uncertainty estimation capabilities of Monte Carlo Dropout, specifically through the estimation of predictive entropy. We will evaluate this method on the CIFAR-10-C dataset, which contains real-world images corrupted with noise, and compare its performance to existing confidence-based and noise-robust methods.
CONTROLS: LeCun, Noise Correcting Autoencoders
COST: 31680
PREDICTION: We expect our confidence-based sample selection method to outperform or match the performance of existing noise-robust methods, especially under high levels of label noise. However, our method may fail if the network's confidence estimates are overly unreliable or biased.

PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of adversarial training with noise-robust loss functions to enhance model robustness in the presence of label noise. We will evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on the CIFAR-100-C dataset, which contains real-world images corrupted with label noise.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Novel Robust Loss Formulation for Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: We propose a robust loss formulation, called LabelNoise Evolution (LNE), that enhances our current understanding of loss functions and noise evolution in noisy label scenarios. Inspired by uncertainty-aware loss functions, LNE evolves the loss function iteratively using predictions from previous iterations and estimates of noise levels. We employ Bayesian neural networks and expect them to learn to adapt to the noise-induced uncertainty over the training process.
CONTROLS: Compare against the widely used Cross-Entropy (CE) loss, as well as Ranger and some other robust loss formulations.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: By exploring label noise evolution, LNE might deliver competitive performance on noisy label datasets, especially with instance-dependent noise; however, it may face challenges in optimizing the noise adaptation process over its continuous iterations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample-Weighting with Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: We develop an uncertainty-aware sample-weighting method for noisy labels, utilizing ensembles of predictions on input samples to generate confidence scores. These confidence scores guide the computation of weight for each sample during training. We believe this uncertainty-based weighting will effectively mitigate the impact of noisy labels while maintaining robustness to instance-dependent noise.
CONTROLS: This method will be compared against reweighting based on sample's loss or Cross-Entropy loss alone.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: With the ability to leverage model uncertainty, sample-weighting with uncertainty estimation may complement label correction methods and achieve better noising-robustness trade-offs; nevertheless, there's a risk of over-reliance on the ensemble, which might amplify model bias present in the local minima of deep neural networks.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED Novorob: Novel Loss Function for Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: We refine our novel loss formulation by incorporating additional objectives that facilitate the combinatorial corrections of instance-dependent noise, namely, discriminating 'clean' instances as irrelevant to the concerned noisy label class. In the spirit of sum-of-regularizers formulations, the revised loss combines margin-based loss to enhance confidence and corrected-loss enhancements. This variant, Novorob, has been designed to reduce difficulties associated with constant labelling quality.
CONTROLS: Compare the updated Novorob formulation against updated CE, Ranger, and Robust LNE from proposal 1, including their performance under increasing noisy label ratios.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: Since Novorob aims at optimizing noise-evolution under increased margin, we may see significant improvements in learning clean labels and resisting instance-dependent labelling noise; if not tuned effectively, the additional objectives might risk either disturbing a possibly effectively learned model's distribution than harm.

Note: I revised the first proposal since our companion strategy, LNE, mirrored substance already suggested reloser formulations.
