ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Component Interaction Analysis for Multi-Label Learning (ACIAL-M)
PROPOSAL: ACIAL-M is an adaptive method to analyze and mitigate potential adverse interactions among training components. We implement a multi-component bottleneck analysis framework that models the interplay between augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function. This framework incorporates autoencoders to capture static and dynamic dependencies across components. During training, ACIAL-M assesses and adapts the configuration by leveraging the learned dependencies to reject harmful interactions and enhance signal preservation.
CONTROLS: We evaluate ACIAL-M in combination with Dyna-MOLC (proposed in turn 1) and compare it to Dyna-MOLC alone and static configurations on the same four benchmarks as before. We measure performance using the same metrics as in turn 1.
COST:  2250
PREDICTION: ACIAL-M enables long-term interaction-heavy configurations to be considered in training, avoiding degradations that arise due to combinations of suboptimal choices. ACIAL-M inserts higher variance in training that is only attainable if Dyna-MOLC is allowed to select locally optimal control policies rather than practiyicing better local and global practise explore.

TITLE: Online Active Learning for Improving Dyna-MOLC Configurations
PROPOSAL: Building on the adaptive framework of Dyna-MOLC, we develop an online active learning mechanism to select a subset of validation instances that are most relevant to the current configuration, and request expert labels (i.e., human or model labels) to refine the configuration. We use a novel trust-aware active learning strategy [1] to determine which instances to select for human labeling. The goal is to focus human labeling efforts on the most informative samples that can help improve the model performance.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the proposed online active learning mechanism combined with Dyna-MOLC on the four benchmarks from turn 1, using a combination of model-based evaluation metrics and human evaluation metrics such as label accuracy and configuration efficiency.
COST:  2750
PREDICTION: The proposed online active learning mechanism significantly improves the quality of Dyna-MOLC's configurations, leading to better performance on validation sets and accelerated training speed. However, the increased reliance on human or model labels might require more resources and involve additional human effort.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Label-Wise Risk Estimation for Barren Multi-Label Thresholds
PROPOSAL: To address the class imbalance issues in multi-label learning, we propose a novel label-wise risk estimation (LRx) technique that dynamically adjusts the loss function to focus on the most challenging labels. LRx models the risk of each label using a Bayesian neural network (BNN) and incorporates the estimated risk into the loss function. The goal is to adaptively adjust the loss function to prioritize the class-balanced learning of all labels.
CONTROLS: We compare LRx with Dyna-MOLC and ACIAL-M on four challenging multi-label classification datasets (CUB-200-2011,Stanford Cars, ImageNet-21K and NUS-WIDE), measuring performance using the overall accuracy, macro F1 score, and class-imbalanced metrics such as precision-recall curves and area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC).
COST:  1529.5
PREDICTION: The proposed LRx technique effectively addresses the class imbalance issue in multi-label learning, leading to improved performance on tail labels and overall accuracy. However, the additional computation cost of estimating risk for each label might make it less efficient on large-scale datasets.

PROPOSAL: To further improve the search efficiency of Dyna-MOLC and ACIAL-M, we propose a niching optimization technique that exploits the geometric properties of the configuration space. The approach, inspired by evolutionary optimization, dynamically creates and manages "niches" in the configuration space where promising combinations of components can evolve. This technique encourages the exploration of diverse configurations and helps to escape local optima.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the proposed niching optimization technique on a range of multi-label classification tasks, including those with complex inter- and intra-label relationships. TITLE: Thermal-Inverse Approach for Discovering Novel Multi-Label Classifiers
PROPOSAL: To discover novel and high-performance multi-label classifiers, we propose a thermal-inverse approach that leverages the success of the "thermal" training strategy, which involves annealing the model's temperature to improve the evaluation of its performance in terms of a suitable metric, and "inverting" the most successful thermal process to discover new configurations. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dyna-MOLC: Adaptive Multi-Label Learning with Phaser Model and Multi-Fidelity Training
PROPOSAL: Dyna-MOLC is a novel adaptive optimization framework designed to dynamically adjust the configuration of core training components (data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function) over the course of multi-label image classification. We incorporate a Phaser model [1], which estimates the evolving probability distribution of label co-occurrences, class difficulties, and feature-label mappings, allowing us to adjust the configuration accordingly. Dyna-MOLC explores the search space using multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization [2]. This combines greedy interleaving of static augmentations with learned optimism and a grid search at each phase. This strategy avoids the combinatorial explosion inherent in exhaustive configuration search.
CONTROLS: We compare Dyna-MOLC with the static configuration paradigm on four popular multi-label image classification benchmarks (NUS-WIDE, OK-VIPER, Flickr8k and IAPR TC-12) [3] and measure performance using the mean average precision (MAP), precision at 1%, 5%, and 10% recall (P1%, P5%, P10%) and precision- recall curve (PRC). We also evaluate the convergent rate and stability by retaining the last epoch and computing rank-one singular value of the output kernels.
COST:  4000
PREDICTION: Dyna-MOLC demonstrates better performance, significantly reducing training instability, faster convergence, and more robust handling of rare labels compared to static configurations. It outperforms the state-of-the-art MAP by at least 5 points across all benchmarks. Failure might occur when estimating the evolving label distributions, leading to misconfiguration and degraded performance.

TITLE: Adaptive Component Interaction Analysis for Multi-Label Learning (ACIAL-M)
PROPOSAL: ACIAL-M is an adaptive method to analyze and mitigate potential adverse interactions among training components. We implement a multi-component bottleneck analysis framework that models the interplay between augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function. This framework incorporates autoencoders to capture static and dynamic dependencies across components. During training, ACIAL-M assesses and adapts the configuration by leveraging the learned dependencies to reject harmful interactions and enhance signal preservation.

TITLE: Online Active Learning for Improving Dyna-MOLC Configurations
PROPOSAL: Building on the adaptive framework of Dyna-MOLC, we develop an online active learning mechanism to select a subset of validation instances that are most relevant to the current configuration, and request expert labels (i.e., human or model labels) to refine the configuration. We use a novel trust-aware active learning strategy [1] to determine which instances to select for human labeling. TITLE: Label-Wise Risk Estimation for Barren Multi-Label Thresholds
PROPOSAL: To address the class imbalance issues in multi-label learning, we propose a novel label-wise risk estimation (LRx) technique that dynamically adjusts the loss function to focus on the most challenging labels. LRx models the risk of each label using a Bayesian neural network (BNN) and incorporates the estimated risk into the loss function. The goal is to adaptively adjust the loss function to prioritize the class-balanced learning of all labels.
CONTROLS: We compare LRx with Dyna-MOLC and ACIAL-M on four challenging multi-label classification datasets (CUB-200-2011,Stanford Cars, ImageNet-21K and NUS-WIDE), measuring performance using the overall accuracy, macro F1 score, and class-imbalanced metrics such as precision-recall curves and area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC).

PROPOSAL: To further improve the search efficiency of Dyna-MOLC and ACIAL-M, we propose a niching optimization technique that exploits the geometric properties of the configuration space. The approach, inspired by evolutionary optimization, dynamically creates and manages "niches" in the configuration space where promising combinations of components can evolve. This technique encourages the exploration of diverse configurations and helps to escape local optima.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating Inter-componemnt Interactions in Adaptive Configuration Tuning
PROPOSAL: Design an extensive experimentation campaign on a dataset such as NUS-WIDE (or a similar multi-label image classification dataset), to study the inter-component interactions in adaptive configuration tuning. Train different ResNet-50 models using various adaptation mechanisms, and systematically vary the training parameters (augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function) to assess how they individually and collectively affect the model's performance and stability. Utilize dimensionality reduction techniques (e.g. PCA) and correlation matrices to visualize and quantify the interactions among different components.
CONTROLS:  Compare with state-of-the-art single-component adaptive methods (e.g., adaptive augmentation, cyclical learning rate schedules) and ablate the adaptation mechanisms to isolate their effects.
COST: 15.295  GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This investigation should provide valuable insights into the highly complex interplay among the training components, helping to pinpoint the optimal adaptation strategies for real-world applications. Potential setbacks might include diagnosing and addressing the increased complexity of adaptive methods, identifying suboptimal combinations of parameters that impair performance, and ensuring interpretability of the results.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Transfer Learning-based Prior-initialized Adaptive Configuration Tuning
PROPOSAL: Implement a transfer learning approach to pretrain a neural network on a large dataset (e.g., ImageNet) and use this pretraining as a prior to improve the speed and effectiveness of the adaptive configuration tuning process. Specifically, initialize the learning parameters, augmentation, optimizer, and schedulers with pre-training-influenced preferences, which improves stability and paves the way for precise adaptation during fine-tuning on the target dataset. Observe the progression of configuration space optimization from this pre-initialized adaptive baseline and track differences from the completely random initialization of adaptive tuning as seen before.
CONTROLS:  Compare with fully random and manually-tuned baseline models, as well as a knowledge distillation approach where a teacher model learns from a pre-trained weight as the prior for the student model.
COST: 36  GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Given that pretraining can provide a robust foundation for multi-label image classification, we expect that the transfer learning-based prior-initialized approach will not only maintain, but also amplify the effectiveness of adaptive configuration tuning, allowing for both faster and more adaptive optimization of hyperparameters. However, the oversight here lies in the very large pretraining dataset, to which variations among images may negatively influence classification accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Calibration for Heavy-Tailed Activations in 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial loss function that guides the calibration set generation towards mitigating the effects of heavy-tailed activation statistics associated with data-independent special tokens in billion-scale 3D reconstruction transformers. Specifically, a generator network creates calibration samples aimed at reducing the heavy tails, and a discriminator differentiates whether the generated samples are representative of the original distribution or not. The generator's goal is to fool the discriminator, and this competition drives the generator towards producing diverse and well-distributed calibration samples. By contrast, the discriminator is updated to recognize and reject samples that fail to represent the real distribution.
CONTROLS: Investigation with baseline calibration methods like the moving average of activations and data augmentation to compare their performance against the adversarial approach; ablation studies to identify the impact of the generator and discriminator architectures on the quality of the calibration set.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The proposed adversarial calibration method significantly reduces the heavy tails of activation statistics, leading to more accurate post-training quantization with a standard deviation reduction of 50% and an 18% gain in camera pose accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Smart Optimistic Lower Bounds for Quantization Ranges
PROPOSAL: Derive a smart optimistic lower bound (SOLO) framework for quantization ranges in 3D reconstruction transformers. SOLO iteratively refines the quantization ranges by utilizing a combination of statistical moment matching and density ratio estimation. It starts with a minimum set of parameters to collect a sufficient number of samples from the calibration set and estimates the distribution moments using robust statistical estimators. Then, it learns a density ratio function to integrate and provide a pessimistic estimation for the tail probabilities, alongside moments of higher orders, leading to the estimation of tighter lower bounds. The process recurrently refines the lower bounds using these estimations to get the most optimized quantization ranges. 
CONTROLS: Analyze and compare SOLO against both linear and linear-log quantization methods, as well as other established lower bound estimation methods like moment bit analysis and transformed weighted histogram, to showcase the effectiveness in capturing activations' distribution and providing accurate representation of lower bounds.
COST: 734
PREDICTION: The proposed smart optimistic lower bounds for quantization ranges lead to improved representation and lower bound estimates by a factor of 2.5 compared to state-of-the-art methods, resulting in at least 10% higher performance and reduced memory usage in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Attention-Aware Pruning for 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: Develop a pruning approach specifically designed for 3D reconstruction transformers that also takes into account the attention mechanisms. The method consists of first computing the sensitivity score of each model parameter using a combination of gradient-based and magnitude-based approaches, then ranking them and identifying the least important ones. During the pruning step, some of these parameters correspond to the special tokens' input weights, propagating sparsity to the data-independent special tokens, and follow this by constructing a new transformer layer with restored weights being adjacent, making the weight exchange process efficient. 
CONTROLS: Compare the attention-aware pruning with state-of-the-art pruning methods like magnitude pruning and threshold-based pruning on standard 3D reconstruction benchmarks, exploring the potential regression in camera pose estimation when missing special tokens' input weights due to sparsity are not paid attention to and left to the nodes' current states. Also analyze the maintained shape inferences beyond trajectories vs pruning ratio in proposed methods in an extensive investigation and shorter pass- framework analyses.
COST: 1035
PREDICTION: The proposed attention-aware pruning outperforms previous methods in terms of accuracy and FLOPs reduction ratio for 3D reconstruction tasks, up to 32% with 15% increase in accuracy, demonstrating the importance of considering attention in pruning 3D reconstruction transformers.

PROPOSAL: Develop a data-driven approach to quantify calibration set selection using synthetic realism. We will leverage synthetic reconstruction data as an intermediary step to identify key patterns and features present in real-world data. Specifically, we will generate a large set of synthetic reconstruction scenarios to simulate real-world variability, and then utilize an autoencoder to identify the most representative scenarios. The encoder will be trained on the synthetic data, while the decoder is trained on the real-world data. We will then select calibration samples based on the similarity between synthetic and real-world data representations.

TITLE: Data-Driven Calibration with Synthetic Realism
PROPOSAL: Develop a data-driven approach to quantify calibration set selection using synthetic realism. We will leverage synthetic reconstruction data as an intermediary step to identify key patterns and features present in real-world data. Specifically, we will generate a large set of synthetic reconstruction scenarios to simulate real-world variability, and then utilize an autoencoder to identify the most representative scenarios. The encoder will be trained on the synthetic data, while the decoder is trained on the real-world data. We will then select calibration samples based on the similarity between synthetic and real-world data representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating 3D Quantization Sensitivity Through Perturbative Analysis
PROPOSAL: We use a series of controlled perturbation experiments to analyze the sensitivity of the VGGT model to quantization noise and its location in the model. Specifically, we examine the performance impact of discrete value fixing in token embeddings (e.g. the camera and register tokens) versus the tokenized image features. We also investigate how varying bit-width and precisions in quantized representations of early and late stages of transformer processing affect overall accuracy in 3D tasks. This approach provides a heuristic for explaining whether successful compression will rely on regularizing the effects of quantization artifacts across each component of the model (e.g. early attention, post-attention fusion), or instead depend on surprisingly selective focusing on suppressive regions in the input images with strongest activation artifacts.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT will be benchmarked against baseline PTQ that uniformly fixed weights to 8-bit or 4-bit values.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The investigation should demonstrate that while PTQ performance might suffer non-linearity across different bits or when focusing on specific parts of the network arch, aggregate accuracy might dramatically increase if special tokens are allowed a bit-doubling. However details have the potential to be confusing from focusing solely on absolute accuracy values without proper normalization.

TITLE: Versatile Implicit Quantization for Billion-scale 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel, versatile implicit quantization method that learns to represent the input and hidden states of the transformer as a set of implicit distributions, rather than discrete values. This is achieved through a trainable, differentiable quantization module that outputs the quantization parameters. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on billion-scale 3D transformers, leveraging the strengths of implicit distributions to reduce the quantization noise and improve the accuracy of the model.
CONTROLS: Evaluation will be based on comparisons with original perturbation, Deformable Dynamic Quantization, and Calibration-agnostic Type-conversion-aware Quantization.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: Implicit quantization should provide significant improvements in accuracy and robustness, especially for billion-scale models, by effectively reducing the quantization noise and capturing the underlying distributions of the data.

TITLE: Efficient Mixed Precision Training for Billion-scale 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose a mixed precision training method that efficiently trains billion-scale 3D transformers using a combination of full-precision and low-precision weights. We develop a novel gradient scaling technique that allows us to train the model with lower precision weights while maintaining the accuracy of the full-precision weights. This approach can significantly reduce the computational cost and memory requirements of training billion-scale 3D transformers.
CONTROLS: We will compare our mixed precision training method with full-precision training and PTQ-based quantization methods.
COST: 8310

PROPOSAL: We propose a semi-supervised learning framework for quantization transfer in 3D transformers. Our approach leverages unlabeled data to learn a domain-invariant representation of the quantization noise, which can be transferred across different quantization schemes and datasets. This allows for more efficient and effective quantization transfer, reducing the need for extensive calibration and validation on each new dataset.

PROPOSAL: We propose an automated machine learning (AutoML) approach for quantization optimization in billion-scale 3D transformers. Our method leverages a combination of black-box optimization and gradient-based methods to search for the optimal quantization parameters, which are learned using a mixture of labeled and unlabeled data. This approach enables efficient and effective quantization optimization, reducing the need for extensive manual tuning and experimentation.
CONTROLS: We will compare our AutoML-based approach with traditional manual tuning and other competitive methods.
COST: 60000
PREDICTION: AutoML-based quantization optimization should provide a significant improvement in quantization performance and efficiency, enabling better compression ratios and accuracy in billion-scale 3D transformers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Training with Enhanced Gradient Compensation for Billion-Scale 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: Implement a variant of quantization-aware training that specifically targets the challenges of large-scale 3D reconstruction transformers like VGGT. This method enhances the conventional gradient compensation approach by introducing a learnable transformation module for data-independent special tokens. The learnable module adaptively compensates for the enhanced heavy-tailed distributions caused by these tokens, helping to mitigate information loss during quantization. Furthermore, we'll use a diverse replacement strategy for the special tokens' quantization, exploring the utility of different replacement patterns, such as cycle instead of linear.
CONTROLS: Test the proposed approach against VGGT and baselines such as non-augmented quantization-aware training and PTQ with a minimal nothing calibration set on a diverse set of real-world benchmarks, such as the Colmap 7-scenes dataset and the Bundler 2nd scene dataset for camera pose prediction and point map reconstruction.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed approach avoids amplifying heavy tails and preserves the accuracy of the VGGT; thus, it outperforms all baselines in camera pose estimation (up to 3.5% mAP increase in Colmap 7-scenes) and points regime analysis yields tiny increase over first baselines in 2 other less large trainings regimes. Improvements might fade as complexity of the points map increases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Efficient Calibration Framework for Post-Training Quantization on Complex Multi-View 3D Data
PROPOSAL: Design an efficient calibration framework for post-training quantization (PTQ) specifically tailored for 3D reconstruction models like VGGT. The framework identifies and extracts "supporting samples" from the calibration set that span the major variability of the 3D features and contain valuable insight into the semantics of the visual data. These supporting samples are down-sampled to minimize calibration data usage and yield significant speed-up while generating robust and generalizeable quantization tables, even when exposed to rare outliers.
CONTROLS: Compare our framework against existing calibration strategies and demonstrate its effectiveness and efficiency on VGGT and state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction benchmarks (e.g., SUN3D, NYU Depth V2) in comparison to baselines of variable-sized calibration sets. 
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our calibration strategy improves VGGT's calibration for 3D features recovery from  12 to 4 B/second with only losing very minor 0.5 percentage points of depth accuracy at CAE column based sets, in particular in high-interested areas. There might, however, be remaining exigencies / competitiveness after when using low iamge group matching samples.

TITLE: Efficient Inference for Billion-Scale 3D Transformers using Low-Precision Floating Point Arithmetic
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of low-precision floating point arithmetic for efficient inference on billion-scale 3D transformers. This will involve developing a framework for converting the 3D transformer architecture to use low-precision floats, and then optimizing the resulting inference pipeline to achieve high performance. The goal is to demonstrate that low-precision floating point arithmetic can be used to achieve real-time inference on 3D transformers without sacrificing accuracy.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the framework on VGGT and compare against traditional high-precision float inference methods. Assess its performance on real-world benchmark datasets, including the ScanNet dataset for 3D reconstruction and the Tanks and Temples dataset.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach reduces the computational cost of inference by up to 4x without sacrificing accuracy, making it suitable for real-time applications. However, there may be some trade-offs in terms of precision, which could impact performance in certain scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigation of Channel-Wise Quantization for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: This experiment will investigate the effectiveness of channel-wise quantization for the data-independent special tokens in VGGT. We will modify the quantization framework to leverage the spatial and semantic sharing of the transformer structure, and apply techniques such as group-wise quantization and activation clipping to handle heavy-tailed activation statistics of special tokens. We will compare the accuracy of camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction on a validation set against fixed-point quantization, to assess the trade-off between quantization precision and inference latency.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, ablation studies of group-wise quantization, activation clipping, and without channel-wise quantization.
COST: 1440
PREDICTION: Expect an improvement in accuracy by 2-4% for camera pose estimation, and 1-3% for point map reconstruction, respectively, due to the efficient handling of special token activations, but could fail if overly complex or domain-specific tokens lead to suboptimal quantization.

PROPOSAL: This experiment will explore the effect of calibration set composition on the performance of post-training quantization for VGGT. We will create a suite of datasets with different calibration set sizes, scene complexities, and point cloud diversity, and evaluate the resilience of learned quantization parameters to outliers and the generalization to unseen scenes. Specifically, we will assess whether augmented samples, scene-separated sets, and stratified sampling can improve the robustness of quantization to calibration set variations.
CONTROLS: Calibration sets with varying sizes, complexities, and diversity, ablation studies of different sampling techniques (augmented, scene-separated, stratified).

PREDICTION: Expect an improvement in robustness to calibration set variations by 10-20%, using stratified sampling, especially for complex scenes, but could fail if point cloud diversity is not a key characteristic of the scene.

TITLE: Multi-Bit Quantization for Variable-Accuracy Applications
PROPOSAL: This experiment will propose a two-stage quantization scheme for VGGT, which alternates between high-accuracy quantization for important views and views with uncertain geometry, and low-accuracy quantization for redundant and well-reconstructed views. We will develop a multibit quantization framework with a learned bit-allocation strategy that leverages spatial context and semantic dependencies within the views, and evaluate the performance on tasks requiring variable-accuracy outputs.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, ablation studies of multi-bit quantization, view selection strategies.
COST: 2880
PREDICTION: Expect a 5-10% improvement in point map reconstruction accuracy for views with high geometric relevance, at the expense of slight degradation (1-2%) in point map accuracy for redundant views, but could fail if the multi-bit quantization strategy overestimates or underestimates the importance of individual views.

TITLE: Multi-Bit Quantization for Variable-Accuracy Applications
PROPOSAL: This experiment will propose a two-stage quantization scheme for VGGT, which alternates between high-accuracy quantization for important views and views with uncertain geometry, and low-accuracy quantization for redundant and well-reconstructed views. We will develop a multibit quantization framework with a learned bit-allocation strategy that leverages spatial context and semantic dependencies within the views, and evaluate the performance on tasks requiring variable-accuracy outputs.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, ablation studies of multi-bit quantization, view selection strategies.
COST: 25920
PREDICTION: Expect a 5-10% improvement in point map reconstruction accuracy for views with high geometric relevance, at the expense of slight degradation (1-2%) in point map accuracy for redundant views, but could fail if the multi-bit quantization strategy overestimates or underestimates the importance of individual views.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-Based Optimization for Label-Smoothing and Quantization Scheduling
PROPOSAL: This experiment will leverage gradient-based optimization to jointly optimize label-smoothing parameters and quantization schedules for VGGT. We will formulate the learning problem as an adversarial game between the quantization network and the VGGT, and use gradient ascent/descent to optimize the trade-off between quantization accuracy and robustness to calibration set variations. We will evaluate the performance on camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, label smoothing with fixed parameters, baseline VGGT without gradient-based optimization.
COST: 3372
PREDICTION: Expect an improvement in camera pose estimation accuracy of 3-5% and point map reconstruction accuracy of 2-4%, due to the adaptive optimization of label smoothing and quantization, but could fail if the gradient-based optimization leads to oscillations or fails to find adequate local optima.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Region-of-Interest (ROI) Quantization for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: This experiment will investigate a Region-of-Interest (ROI) quantization approach for VGGT, where we identify the most informative regions in the input frames and apply coarse-grained quantization to those regions. We will develop a ROI selection strategy that leverages channel attentions and semantic dependencies, and evaluate its performance on camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Abalone studies of ROI selection strategies, without ROI quantization, fixed-point quantization.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: Expect a 5-10% improvement in memory usage and up to 2% speed-up in inference time without compromising model accuracy, depending on the ROI selection strategy, but could fail if the selected ROIs are not representative of the relevant features for the task.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: 3D Scan-Specific Quantization for Variable-Complexity Scenes
PROPOSAL: This experiment will develop a scene-aware quantization strategy that adaptively adjusts the quantization bit-width based on the complexity of the current scene, leveraging 3D scan-specific features and semantic context. We will train a separate predictor network to estimate the scene complexity and integrate it with the quantization schedule, aiming to improve the robustness and generalizability of VGGT for a wide range of 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, ablation studies of scene-aware features, complexity estimation methods, and without scene-aware quantization.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: Expect an improvement in accuracy of 3-5% on more complex scenes and up to 10% on simpler scenes, by adaptively adjusting the quantization bit-width based on the scene complexity, but could fail if the complexity estimator is not robust or the integration with the quantization schedule leads to poor performance in certain edge cases.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning of Quantization Parameters Across Scenes and Tasks
PROPOSAL: This experiment will investigate the transferability of quantization parameters learned from one scene or task to another, with the goal of reducing the need for extensive calibration sets and improving the generalizability of VGGT for 3D reconstruction. We will develop a meta-learning framework to learn a shared representation of quantization parameters across a variety of scenes and tasks, and evaluate its performance on unseen scenes and tasks.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, ablation studies of meta-learning frameworks, transfer learning methods, and without transfer learning.
COST: 8640
PREDICTION: Expect a 5-15% improvement in accuracy on unseen scenes and tasks, due to the shared representation of quantization parameters learned through meta-learning, but could fail if the meta-learning framework is not robust or the transfer learning leads to catastrophic forgetting of important quantization patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Framework for Multi-Bit and Multi-Scale Quantization in VGGT
PROPOSAL: This experiment will develop a unified framework to integrate multi-bit and multi-scale quantization techniques within VGGT. We will propose a novel architecture that combines hierarchical channel-wise quantization with ROI-aware quantization and transfer learning-based quantization, and experimentally evaluate its performance on camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline VGGT, multi-bit quantization, multi-scale ROI-aware quantization, single-scale ROI-aware quantization, fixed-point quantization.
COST: 10560
PREDICTION: Expect a 10-20% improvement in accuracy and up to 50% improvement in memory efficiency, by leveraging the strengths of multiple quantization techniques and architectures, but could fail if the integration leads to overfitting or poor convergence across various quantization settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigation of Channel-Wise Quantization for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: This experiment will investigate the effectiveness of channel-wise quantization for the data-independent special tokens in VGGT. We will modify the quantization framework to leverage the spatial and semantic sharing of the transformer structure, and apply techniques such as group-wise quantization and activation clipping to handle heavy-tailed activation statistics of special tokens. We will compare the accuracy of camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction on a validation set against fixed-point quantization, to assess the trade-off between quantization precision and inference latency.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, ablation studies of group-wise quantization, activation clipping, and without channel-wise quantization.
COST: 4320
PREDICTION: Expect an improvement in accuracy by 2-4% for camera pose estimation, and 1-3% for point map reconstruction, respectively, due to the efficient handling of special token activations, but could fail if overly complex or domain-specific tokens lead to suboptimal quantization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analysis of Calibration Set Composition for Multi-View 3D Data
PROPOSAL: This experiment will explore the effect of calibration set composition on the performance of post-training quantization for VGGT. We will create a suite of datasets with different calibration set sizes, scene complexities, and point cloud diversity, and evaluate the resilience of learned quantization parameters to outliers and the generalization to unseen scenes. Specifically, we will assess whether augmented samples, scene-separated sets, and stratified sampling can improve the robustness of quantization to calibration set variations.
CONTROLS: Calibration sets with varying sizes, complexities, and diversity, ablation studies of different sampling techniques (augmented, scene-separated, stratified).
COST: 6480
PREDICTION: Expect an improvement in robustness to calibration set variations by 10-20%, using stratified sampling, especially for complex scenes, but could fail if point cloud diversity is not a key characteristic of the scene.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Analysis of Calibration Set Composition for Multi-View 3D Data
PROPOSAL: This experiment will revise the original proposal by incorporating feature-perceptability-aware sampling for stratified sampling, where instead of sampling based on the input images, we sample based on the distributively-perceptable features, to improve the convergence of the learned quantization parameters. We will compare the resulting quantization parameter convergence with traditional stratified sampling and ablate individual components to identify meaningful improvements.
CONTROLS: Stratified sampling with feature-perceptability-aware sampling, traditional stratified sampling, ablation studies of individual components.
COST: 10800 (revised from 6480)
PREDICTION: Expect a more stable convergence of learned quantization parameters, especially in scenarios where there are complex and diverse scenes, but could fail if the chosen perceptability-aware features don't accurately represent the problem domain.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigation of Channel-Wise Quantization for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: This revised experiment will explore a hierarchical channel-wise quantization strategy for special tokens, where the bit-width selection is based on the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the distribution over special token activations. We will incorporate a learnable thresholding function and monitor the quantization error as a function of the number of quantization bits and threshold level, aiming to find the optimal trade-off between accuracy and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Fixed-point quantization, ablation studies of hierarchical channel-wise quantization, learned thresholding function, and threshold values.
COST: 9360 (revised from 4320)
PREDICTION: Expect a 10-20% improvement in accuracy for camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction tasks, with up to 4 bits of quantization, but could fail if the hierarchical strategy overestimates the quantization range for high-entropy channels.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Quantization-aware Training for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the application of quantization-aware training (QAT) to VGGT, as an alternative to PTQ. In QAT, we will modify VGGT's architecture to use mixed precision during training, with a small set of calibration tokens that track the evolution of quantization errors. We will train VGGT on a large-scale 3D dataset, such as DTU, using mixed precision and compute the corresponding forward and backwards pass activations. This process will help us estimate the optimal weights and quantization ranges that minimize the overall quantization error on the target 3D reconstruction task. We will then compare QAT against PTQ on the VGGT 3D reconstruction task and monitor how these two paradigms affect calibration error.
CONTROLS: Baseline: PTQ on VGGT; PTQ with sampling
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: We expect that QAT would demonstrate improved performance on the VGGT 3D reconstruction task, with lower calibration error compared to PTQ, but with increased computational costs due to the need to compute the quantization errors during training. The potential failure might be the increased sensitivity of QAT to hyperparameters selection, which could make it harder to converge to a global optimum.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analysis of PTQ Limitations on Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a thorough analysis of PTQ limitations on the special tokens used in VGGT, particularly focusing on the heavy-tailed, high-variance activation distributions. We will use the following methods: (i) examining the impact of clipping on the distribution shapes, (ii) comparing different quantization schemes (e.g., MinMax, MeanStd), (iii) analyzing outliers in the calibration set. This empirical analysis will provide insights into why PTQ might struggle with special tokens and help us identify the key factors that affect the quantization performance on these tokens.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard PTQ on VGGT; PTQ with clipping; PTQ with MinMax quantization
COST: 1500

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration Set Selection for PTQ on VGGT
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of calibration set selection on the performance of PTQ on VGGT. We will experiment with different calibration set sizes, strategies for sampling diverse scenes, and methods for augmenting the calibration set (e.g., random perturbations, data augmentation). The goal is to discover which calibration sets allow PTQ to effectively capture the high-dimensional semantic space of VGGT and generalize to unseen scenes.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard PTQ on VGGT; random sampling; data augmentation; diverse scene sampling
COST: 2100

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmented Sampling for Calibration Set Generation
PROPOSAL: To improve the efficacy of calibration set selection, we will introduce an augmented sampling approach by injecting multimodal augmentations (e.g., photometric transformations, geometry-based augmentations) into the calibration set. This augmentation will help increase the representativeness of the calibration set and reduce the impact of data shortage on PTQ performance. We will evaluate the performance of augmented sampling through a comprehensive comparison with a variety of sampling strategies, including random sampling, diverse scene sampling, and data augmentation.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard PTQ on VGGT; standard calibration set selection; random sampling; diverse scene sampling; data augmentation
COST: 2400

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Exploring Quantization-aware Training for VGGT (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We will modify the architecture of VGGT to adaptively adjust the quantization scheme during training, depending on the frequency of activation updates. Specifically, we will design an additional quantization-control module that dynamically weights the contribution of low-precision and high-precision weights to the overall optimization objective. By using this adaptive approach, we aim to mitigate the limitations of PTQ and improve the overall quantization performance. We will train the revised VGGT model on a large-scale 3D dataset and compare its performance against PTQ and the original VGGT model.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard PTQ on VGGT; PTQ with adaptive quantization-control module; original VGGT model
COST: 3000

TITLE: Quantization-aware Attention Masking for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We will extend our previous approach to adaptively adjust the quantization scheme for VGGT by introducing attention-aware masking of activations during training. This masking will discard the highest-frequency activations that contribute the least to the decision-making process, thus reducing the impact of high-frequency noise on quantization performance. We will train a modified VGGT model that incorporates this attention-aware masking scheme and compare its performance against the original model and PTQ-based approaches.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard PTQ on VGGT; original VGGT model; VGGT with adaptive quantization-control module
COST: 3600

TITLE: Calibration Set Selection for PTQ on VGGT (Revised)
PROPOSAL: We will refine the calibration set selection approach for PTQ by integrating a stream-based active learning strategy. In this strategy, we will select a subset of calibration samples that provide the most informative updates to the PTQ model, enabling more efficient exploration of the high-dimensional space of VGGT's special tokens. We will use uncertainty sampling to identify the most uncertain samples and validate our approach using a combination of real-world and synthetic data.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard PTQ on VGGT; standard calibration set selection; active learning with uncertainty sampling; PTQ with augmented sampling approach

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sanity Check for PTQ-induced Regression Errors
PROPOSAL: To quantify the impact of PTQ-induced regression errors, we will analyze the bias and variance of our results obtained using PTQ-based VGGT and compare them against results obtained using calibrated VGGT. We will measure the residuals between PTQ-based VGGT and calibrated VGGT outputs and execute regression analysis to determine whether the differences in accuracy are statistically significant. If PTQ-based VGGT introduces significant regression errors, we will revisit previous experiments and consider alternative solutions such as repeat calibration or adjustment of calibration set diversity.
CONTROLS: Baseline: calibrated VGGT; PTQ-based VGGT; sensitivity analysis of regression errors
COST: 6600

We will measure the residuals between PTQ-based VGGT and calibrated VGGT outputs and execute regression analysis to determine whether the differences in accuracy are statistically significant. If PTQ-based VGGT introduces significant regression errors, we will revisit previous experiments and consider alternative solutions such as repeat calibration or adjustment of calibration set diversity.
CONTROLS: Baseline: calibrated VGGT; PTQ-based VGGT; sensitivity analysis of regression errors
COST: 60000

TITLE: Exploring Quantization-aware Training for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the application of quantization-aware training (QAT) to VGGT, as an alternative to PTQ. In QAT, we will modify VGGT's architecture to use mixed precision during training, with a small set of calibration tokens that track the evolution of quantization errors. We will train VGGT on a large-scale 3D dataset, such as DTU, using mixed precision and compute the corresponding forward and backwards pass activations. This process will help us estimate the optimal weights and quantization ranges that minimize the overall quantization error on the target 3D reconstruction task. We will then compare QAT against PTQ on the VGGT 3D reconstruction task and monitor how these two paradigms affect calibration error.
CONTROLS: Baseline: PTQ on VGGT; PTQ with sampling
COST: 8100

The potential failure might be the increased sensitivity of QAT to hyperparameters selection, which could make it harder to converge to a global optimum.

PROPOSAL: We will conduct a thorough analysis of PTQ limitations on the special tokens used in VGGT, particularly focusing on the heavy-tailed, high-variance activation distributions. We will use the following methods: (i) examining the impact of clipping on the distribution shapes, (ii) comparing different quantization schemes (e.g., MinMax, MeanStd), (iii) analyzing outliers in the calibration set. This empirical analysis will provide insights into why PTQ might struggle with special tokens and help us identify the key factors that affect the quantization performance on these tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable DPT for In-Context Reinforcement Learning in Multi-Domain Continuous-Control Tasks
PROPOSAL:  Implement a novel variant of DPT, dubbed "DPT-VF", which incorporates a value-function (VF) encoder to capture complex observation and action dependencies in multi-task continuous-control environments. Specifically, we condition the DPT's action decoder on a learned VF representation, obtained via a separate neural network that processes the observation space. This setup enables the model to efficiently adapt to novel tasks, leveraging the encoded VF as context for in-context learning.
CONTROLS: Compare to vanilla DPT, DPT with a fixed, pre-trained VF, and a baseline model that uses a separate policy network for each task.
COST: 50
PREDICTION: DPT-VF will show improved in-context adaptation performance over vanilla DPT and the fixed-VF variant on a broad range of continuous-control tasks in multiple domains, with lower test-time inference latency; however, its success will depend on the quality of the learned VF estimator.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning Action Distributions with Neural Variational Flow
PROPOSAL: Develop a neural variational flow (NVF) model to represent the complex action distributions arising in multi-domain continuous-control tasks. The NVF will learn to map a lower-dimensional latent space, induced by the contrasting property of the action decoder, to a high-dimensional action space, enabling expressive modeling of multi-modal continuous action posteriors. At inference time, NVF will enable the sampling of realistic and diverse action trajectories.
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard normal distribution action prior, a learned Gaussian mixture model, and an adversarial generative model.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The NVF-based DPT variant will exhibit improved in-context policy generalization and sampling efficiency compared to baseline action distribution models, especially on unseen tasks with complex action spaces; however, its evaluation will be sensitive to the choice of hyperparameters and flow graphs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context-Aware Exploration for Scalable DPT in Multi-Domain Continuous-Control Tasks
PROPOSAL: Design a simple yet effective exploration strategy to leverage in-context learning capabilities of DPT in continuous-control environments. This strategy, called "context-aware exploration" (CAE), will iteratively refine the in-context dataset by incorporating observations and actions obtained through guided exploration, which exploits the knowledge distilled from the DPT's learned action distributions. CAE will adapt to task dynamics and encourage the model to explore novel regions of the action space.
CONTROLS: Compare to an epsilon-greedy exploration strategy, maximum entropy reinforcement learning, and a curriculum learning-based exploration method.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: CAE will enable the scalable DPT to improve in-context adaptation speed and efficiency in novel tasks with complex dynamics and action spaces, while reducing the need for extensive fine-tuning; however, its success may rely on the choice of exploration parameters and the distributional consistency of the in-context dataset.

This transfer learning approach will leverage a learned latent embedding of tasks to share information between tasks, augmenting the in-context learning capabilities of the scalable DPT and improving its ability to adapt to new, unseen environments.
CONTROLS: Compare to a technique using task-agnostic meta-learning, offline reinforcement learning, and transfer learning between closely related tasks.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: The value function transfer learning-based scalable DPT will exhibit notable improvements in adapting to novel tasks with reduced training samples, especially when the tasks share common structures and components; however, its success will depend on the quality of the task embeddings and the ability to balance the transfer of knowledge across related tasks.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Learning Dynamic Action Distributions with Neural Variational Flow and Competing Expertise
PROPOSAL: Enhance the neural variational flow (NVF) model by incorporating competing expertise to capture task-dependent action distributions and adapt to changing task dynamics. This can be achieved through a hierarchical learning setup where multiple NVF experts, each tailored to a specific task dimension, jointly represent the complex action space. At inference time, this multi-expert NVF model will provide a more comprehensive and task-adaptive action distribution, enabling the scalable DPT to better generalize to unseen tasks and environments.
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard NVF model, a learned Gaussian mixture model with competing expertise, and an adversarial generative model with task-adaptive action representations.
COST: 1080
PREDICTION: The multi-expert NVF variant will demonstrate notable improvements in capturing dynamic task-dependent action distributions and adapting to changing task dynamics, leading to better in-context policy generalization and sampling efficiency, especially when the tasks exhibit complex and evolving action spaces; however, its complexity and potential for overfitting may require careful tuning and regularization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Hierarchical Sampling for Scalable DPT in Multi-Domain Continuous-Control Tasks
PROPOSAL: Design a novel hierarchical sampling strategy to efficiently explore the action space and accelerate the search for optimal policies in multi-domain continuous-control tasks. This strategy, called "Hierarchical Sampling per Trajectory" (HST), will utilize the hierarchical state-action embeddings learned by the scalable DPT to partition the action space and sequentially sample from the most informative regions. The HST will adapt to the complexity of the task and the characteristics of the action distribution, enabling the scalable DPT to find near-optimal policies more efficiently.
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard uniform sampling strategy, a learned policy-based exploration strategy, and a trajectory-based exploration method with adaptive sampling rates.
COST: 960
PREDICTION: The HST-based scalable DPT will exhibit significant improvements in policy discovery efficiency and explore-exploit trade-off, especially when the tasks have complex action spaces and require adaptive sampling strategies; however, its effectiveness may be sensitive to the choice of hierarchical partitioning and the learned state-action embeddings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Agnostic State Representation Learning for Scalable DPT in Multi-Domain Continuous-Control Tasks
PROPOSAL: Explore a novel approach to learn task-agnostic state representations that can be used across multiple domains and tasks. This can be achieved through an autoencoder-based framework that learns a shared, compact, and informative state embedding space that is invariant to task-specific features. By using this shared state representation, the scalable DPT can generalize more effectively to unseen tasks and environments, and improve its transfer learning capabilities.
CONTROLS: Compare to a task-specific state representation learning approach, a learned policy-based state abstraction method, and an unsupervised feature learning approach with domain-specific adaptability.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The task-agnostic state representation learning-based scalable DPT will exhibit notable improvements in policy generalization, transfer learning, and adaptability across multiple domains and tasks; however, its success will depend on the quality of the learned state embeddings and the ability of the DPT to effectively utilize them.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Hierarchical State-Action Embeddings with Hierarchical Transformers for Scalable DPT in Multi-Domain Continuous-Control Tasks
PROPOSAL: Integrate a hierarchical transformer architecture into the scalable DPT's hierarchical state-action embeddings to further enhance the model's representation learning capabilities. The hierarchical transformer will learn to attend to different levels of abstraction within the state-action space, enabling the model to capture long-range dependencies and relationships between task-specific features. This integration will significantly improve the scalable DPT's ability to generalize across multiple domains and tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare to the original hierarchical state-action embeddings approach, a standard transformer-based state-action representation learning method, and an autoencoder-based state representation learning approach with hierarchical sampling.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The hierarchical transformer-based scalable DPT will exhibit remarkable improvements in policy generalization, transfer learning, and adaptability across multiple domains and tasks, with notable breakthroughs in complex tasks that require capturing long-range dependencies and relationships; however, its complexity and the potential for overfitting may require careful tuning and regularization.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modulating DPT through Residual Learning for Continuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the extension of DPT to continuous action spaces using residual learning to bypass the naivety of the original model in dealing with complex action distributions. We will modify DPT by adding residual connections that access both the policy's previous output and the "knowledge" encoded within the attention context, which in this case is the in-context dataset of state-action pairs. This is implemented through augmenting the feed-forward network of the value function used by DPT across layers and branches where the residual information from previous utterances becomes more complex.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach against a vanilla DPT extended to continuous actions and against a baseline that uses a standard Transformer-based model, similar to variants currently discussed in the literature.
COST: 1830
PREDICTION: Our approach is likely to demonstrate improved performance compared to vanilla DPT and the baseline on robot manipulation tasks, potentially providing an upper bound for in-context learning in these environments, but this does not automatically generalize to large action spaces; there could be limitations in how this approach adapts to the unexplored action spaces in tasks such as autonomous driving.

Private Note: One major point of potential failure arises from the model possibly misinterpreting the feedback from the residual network in certain scenarios, resulting in overfitting the learned action dynamics and consequently, limited generalizability. Also, it could be challenging to establish expert demonstrations due to the technical complexities.

TITLE: Evaluating Multi-Modal Action Posterior Estimation via Hierarchical Normalizing Flows
PROPOSAL: Given the challenge of modeling complex, multi-modal continuous action posteriors, we propose the use of hierarchical normalizing flows to estimate the action posterior distribution in DPT. We will integrate hierarchical normalizing flows into the value function of DPT, enabling the estimation of high-dimensional, complex action distributions in continuous control environments.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach against DPT with residual learning (proposal 1) and evaluate its performance on robot locomotion and humanoid control tasks, both with and without expert demonstrations.
COST: 2531.2
PREDICTION: This combination of normalizing flows can show better performance on environments which require accurately capturing multimodal action posteriors, such as obstacle-laden walking tasks; yet, it's not guaranteed to prevent potential limitations in samples of more complex actions that have been developed too aggressively with too few steps; this potential failure still requires validation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Synthetic Datasets for Pretraining in Multi-Domain Continuous-Action Robotics Tasks
PROPOSAL: To address the limitations of real-world pretraining datasets in multi-domain settings, we will create a suite of synthetic datasets that simulate various robotic tasks with distinct MDP structures and control complexities. These datasets will be used to train a range of models, including our proposed DPT variants and AD, in order to evaluate their pretraining performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare the models' performance on the simulated environments and in real-world multi-domain tasks against their performance on pretraining datasets such as the MetaWorld dataset.
COST: 2100

TITLE: Modulating DPT through Residual Learning for Continuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the extension of DPT to continuous action spaces using residual learning to bypass the naivety of the original model in dealing with complex action distributions. We will modify DPT by adding residual connections that access both the policy's previous output and the "knowledge" encoded within the attention context, which in this case is the in-context dataset of state-action pairs. This is implemented through augmenting the feed-forward network of the value function used by DPT across layers and branches where the residual information from previous utterances becomes more complex.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach against a vanilla DPT extended to continuous actions and against a baseline that uses a standard Transformer-based model, similar to variants currently discussed in the literature.
COST: 5500
PREDICTION: Our approach is likely to demonstrate improved performance compared to vanilla DPT and the baseline on robot manipulation tasks, potentially providing an upper bound for in-context learning in these environments, but this does not automatically generalize to large action spaces; there could be limitations in how this approach adapts to the unexplored action spaces in tasks such as autonomous driving.

Private Note: One major point of potential failure arises from the model possibly misinterpreting the feedback from the residual network in certain scenarios, resulting in overfitting the learned action dynamics and consequently, limited generalizability. Also, it could be challenging to establish expert demonstrations due to the technical complexities.

TITLE: Investigating Multi-Modal Policy Capacity for General-Purpose Reinforcement Learning
PROPOSAL: Extend the Decision Pretrained Transformer (DPT) to model higher-dimensional continuous action spaces and multi-modal policy distributions by incorporating Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) in the output layer. CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the extended DPT (DPT-GMM) to vanilla DPT on a suite of diverse continuous-control environments, including robot manipulation and robot locomotion. Also, include an ablation study on the effect of the number of mixture components and the type of GMMs used.

PREDICTION: Expected to see improved performance in tasks that require the agent to learn multi-modal policies, such as tasks involving obstacle avoidance or navigating through complex environments. Failure could occur if the GMMs lead to overestimation of action variances, hindering the agent's ability to adapt to changing environments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Multi-Modal Policy Capacity for General-Purpose Reinforcement Learning
PROPOSAL: Extend the Decision Pretrained Transformer (DPT) to model higher-dimensional continuous action spaces and multi-modal policy distributions by incorporating Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) in the output layer. The GMMs will allow the agent to represent various action modes through learned mixture components.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the extended DPT (DPT-GMM) to vanilla DPT on a suite of diverse continuous-control environments, including robot manipulation and robot locomotion. Also, include an ablation study on the effect of the number of mixture components and the type of GMMs used.
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved performance in tasks that require the agent to learn multi-modal policies, such as tasks involving obstacle avoidance or navigating through complex environments. Failure could occur if the GMMs lead to overestimation of action variances, hindering the agent's ability to adapt to changing environments.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Scalability of Multi-Modal DPT to Diverse Continuous-Control Tasks
PROPOSAL: Develop a hierarchical DPT (HDPT) architecture, where each sub-policy in the hierarchy is a DPT-GMM (from proposal 1). Train HDPT on a large cross-domain dataset of continuous-control tasks, and evaluate its performance on unseen tasks from various domains, including humanoid control, HVAC control, and building energy management.
CONTROLS: Compare HDPT to AD and vanilla DPT on the same cross-domain dataset and set of unseen tasks. Assess the effect of hierarchy depth and sub-policy complexity on HDPT's performance.
COST: 121000
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved performance on unseen tasks and superior scalability compared to vanilla DPT and AD. Challenges may arise if the added depth and complexity of HDPT make optimization more difficult, hindering its ability to adapt to new tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: In-Context Learning with Hierarchical Task Representation
PROPOSAL: Introduce a task representation module to the HDPT architecture (from proposal 2), allowing it to learn a hierarchical representation of tasks and abstract away from specific details inherent to each environment. This will enable the agent to adapt more flexibly to unseen tasks and retrieve relevant in-context information from the modules' hierarchical structure.
CONTROLS: Include an ablation study on the effect of task representation module granularity and degree of abstraction. Compare the performance of HDPT-T (with task representation) to HDPT without this module on the same set of unseen tasks.
COST: 169000
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved adaptability and robustness to task variations, particularly in environments with complex task structures or sudden changes in the task requirements. Risk of over-reliance on in-context learning could lead to under-exploitation of the agent's learned policies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Customizing Decision Pretrained Transformer for Scale
PROPOSAL:  This experiment adapts the DPT model to better handle complex action spaces in continuous-control reinforcement learning tasks. Specifically, we introduce a novel hierarchical action distribution, composed of multiple vectors that capture low-dimensional, task-specific action features. Each vector is defined by a separate, task-agnostic Transformer layer, ensuring that the encoded features are utilized effectively within the downstream decision-making process. This hierarchical setup enables the model to natively sample complex, multi-modal continuous actions, ensuring the clarity of posterior sampling interpretation.
CONTROLS:  We compare baseline DPT with various action distributions: GP-based distribution (expected action frequencies), Gaussian Fixed distribution and random action for proxy consistency as comparison. We train each action distribution on a diverse set of continuous-control tasks from the robot manipulation and robot locomotion domain.
COST:  300
PREDICTION:  The proposed hierarchical action distribution significantly outperforms baseline DPT, achieving robust in-context learning and posterior sampling behavior on unseen, diverse tasks, while the baseline action distributions fail to do so.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  In-Context Meta-Learning for Task-Agnostic Representation
PROPOSAL:  This experiment proposes a meta-learning framework that leverages DPT to learn a task-agnostic representation, enabling the agent to transfer its knowledge across various domains and tasks. The approach involves treating each task as a prompt and the model as the learner. By iteratively updating the model with in-context learning, it adapts to a wide range of tasks and learns to generate task-specific action distributions that align with the MDP structures of the environment. This allows the agent to cope with the varying observation and action spaces across different tasks.
CONTROLS:  We compare our method to a DPT variant that uses separate Task-learned DPT for each domain. Another baseline uses highly developed, fully Task-learned Transformers which do not transfer outside of trained domain. Additionally, a, fully Trained from Scratch, Mono-task model gets used for ablations analysis, both models used as comparison to task-wise models in controls. We test this approach on a collection of tasks from humanoid control and industrial process control domains.
COST:  400
PREDICTION:  Our meta-learning approach enables the agent to achieve robust in-context learning and transfer its knowledge to unseen tasks across different domains, resulting in improved performance compared to baseline DPT and task-specific DPT variants, with potential discontinuities in improvement that require careful consideration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Bayesian Multi-Modal Inference for DPT
PROPOSAL:  This experiment extends the DPT model to capture complex, multi-modal action posteriors by incorporating a Bayesian neural network, allowing the agent to reason about uncertainty in the decision-making process. We introduce a probabilistic output layer, using a mixture of Gaussians to represent the action distribution. This setup enables the model to capture the multiple modes of the action posterior, improving its ability to adapt to unseen tasks and environments.
CONTROLS:  We compare our Bayesian multi-modal DPT to a standard DPT with a single action vector and a probabilistic DPT variant using a softmax output layer. We also test its performance on a variety of tasks from the robot locomotion domain, where the action space is known to be multi-modal.
COST:  567
PREDICTION:  The Bayesian multi-modal DPT model outperforms its baseline variants in terms of task transfer and exploration capabilities, capturing complex, multi-modal action posteriors and adapting to unseen tasks with greater robustness. However, it may require careful hyperparameter tuning and may not work as well on tasks with single-modal action spaces.

PROPOSAL:  This experiment proposes a multi-fidelity inference framework for the DPT model, allowing it to trade off between precision and complexity when making predictions. PREDICTION:  The multi-fidelity inference framework enables the agent to achieve improved performance and efficiency on tasks with varying requirements, leveraging a hierarchy of models to adapt to changing task demands. However, it may require careful tuning of the framework to achieve optimal performance.

TITLE:  Customizing Decision Pretrained Transformer for Scale
PROPOSAL:  This experiment adapts the DPT model to better handle complex action spaces in continuous-control reinforcement learning tasks. Specifically, we introduce a novel hierarchical action distribution, composed of multiple vectors that capture low-dimensional, task-specific action features. Each vector is defined by a separate, task-agnostic Transformer layer, ensuring that the encoded features are utilized effectively within the downstream decision-making process. This hierarchical setup enables the model to natively sample complex, multi-modal continuous actions, ensuring the clarity of posterior sampling interpretation.
CONTROLS:  We compare baseline DPT with various action distributions: GP-based distribution (expected action frequencies), Gaussian Fixed distribution and random action for proxy consistency as comparison. We train each action distribution on a diverse set of continuous-control tasks from the robot manipulation and robot locomotion domain.
COST:  900
PREDICTION:  The proposed hierarchical action distribution significantly outperforms baseline DPT, achieving robust in-context learning and posterior sampling behavior on unseen, diverse tasks, while the baseline action distributions fail to do so.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  In-Context Meta-Learning for Task-Agnostic Representation
PROPOSAL:  This experiment proposes a meta-learning framework that leverages DPT to learn a task-agnostic representation, enabling the agent to transfer its knowledge across various domains and tasks. The approach involves treating each task as a prompt and the model as the learner. By iteratively updating the model with in-context learning, it adapts to a wide range of tasks and learns to generate task-specific action distributions that align with the MDP structures of the environment. This allows the agent to cope with the varying observation and action spaces across different tasks.
CONTROLS:  We compare our method to a DPT variant that uses separate Task-learned DPT for each domain. Another baseline uses highly developed, fully Task-learned Transformers which do not transfer outside of trained domain. Additionally, a, fully Trained from Scratch, Mono-task model gets used for ablations analysis, both models used as comparison to task-wise models in controls. We test this approach on a collection of tasks from humanoid control and industrial process control domains.
COST:  1200
PREDICTION:  Our meta-learning approach enables the agent to achieve robust in-context learning and transfer its knowledge to unseen tasks across different domains, resulting in improved performance compared to baseline DPT and task-specific DPT variants, with potential discontinuities in improvement that require careful consideration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Bayesian Multi-Modal Inference for DPT
PROPOSAL:  This experiment extends the DPT model to capture complex, multi-modal action posteriors by incorporating a Bayesian neural network, allowing the agent to reason about uncertainty in the decision-making process. We introduce a probabilistic output layer, using a mixture of Gaussians to represent the action distribution. This setup enables the model to capture the multiple modes of the action posterior, improving its ability to adapt to unseen tasks and environments.
CONTROLS:  We compare our Bayesian multi-modal DPT to a standard DPT with a single action vector and a probabilistic DPT variant using a softmax output layer. We also test its performance on a variety of tasks from the robot locomotion domain, where the action space is known to be multi-modal.
COST:  1700
PREDICTION:  The Bayesian multi-modal DPT model outperforms its baseline variants in terms of task transfer and exploration capabilities, capturing complex, multi-modal action posteriors and adapting to unseen tasks with greater robustness. However, it may require careful hyperparameter tuning and may not work as well on tasks with single-modal action spaces.

PROPOSAL:  This revised experiment further refines the Bayesian multi-modal DPT model by incorporating an ensemble of multiple DPT models, each trained on a different subset of the data. This ensemble approach allows the model to leverage the strengths of each individual model and capture a more diverse range of action posteriors, improving its ability to adapt to unseen tasks and environments.
CONTROLS:  We compare our ensemble-based Bayesian multi-modal DPT to the baseline DPT and the single-modal probabilistic DPT variant. We also test its performance on a collection of tasks from the robot manipulation and humanoid control domains, where diverse action spaces are present.

PREDICTION:  The ensemble-based Bayesian multi-modal DPT model achieves significant improvements in task transfer and exploration capabilities, capturing diverse, multi-modal action posteriors and adapting to unseen tasks with greater robustness. PROPOSAL:  This experiment explores the ability of the DPT model to transfer its knowledge across parametric task variations, where the agent must adapt to changes in the environment, such as different controller parameters or varying coefficients in the MDP. By using a domain randomization approach, the model is trained on a range of tasks with differing parameters, allowing it to learn a generalizable representation of the environment.
CONTROLS:  We compare our transfer learning approach to a DPT variant that uses separate task-specific models for each parametric variation. TITLE:  Demonstrative Context Augmentation for DPT
PROPOSAL:  This experiment explores the use of demonstrative context augmentation to enhance the DPT model's performance on unseen tasks. By combining the DPT model with expert demonstrations, the agent can leverage the knowledge of experienced experts to improve its decision-making process. The approach involves training the DPT model on a dataset that includes both the original task and expert demonstrations, allowing the model to learn from both its own experience and the guidance of experts.
CONTROLS:  We compare our demonstrative context augmentation approach to a DPT variant that uses separate models for each task and a baseline DPT that does not use expert demonstrations. We also test its performance on a collection of tasks from the autonomous driving and PDE control domains, where expert demonstrations can significantly aid learning.
COST:  3900
PREDICTION:  The demonstrative context augmentation approach enables the agent to achieve improved performance on unseen tasks, leveraging the knowledge of experts to enhance its decision-making process. However, it may require careful selection and preprocessing of expert demonstrations to ensure effective learning.

PROPOSAL:  This experiment proposes a multi-fidelity inference framework for the DPT model, allowing it to trade off between precision and complexity when making predictions. By leveraging a hierarchy of models with decreasing complexity, the agent can make more efficient use of computational resources and adapt to changing task requirements. This approach involves using a probabilistic neural network to select the most suitable model for each prediction, based on the uncertainty of the input data.
CONTROLS:  We compare our multi-fidelity inference approach to a DPT variant that uses a single model for all task requirements and a baseline DPT that does not use task-specific models. We also test its performance on a collection of tasks from the HVAC control and building energy management domains, where efficient use of computational resources is critical.
COST:  4500
PREDICTION:  The multi-fidelity inference framework enables the agent to achieve improved performance and efficiency on tasks with varying requirements, leveraging a hierarchy of models to adapt to changing task demands. However, it may require careful tuning of the framework to achieve optimal performance.
